385YE Summer Solstice Conclave sessions.d: After the previous summit, 324 mana was shared among the grandmasters, led by the Rod and Shield. New titleholders included Dima Vasilyevna Novosad (Master of the Koboldi), Cassandra i Periera i Erigo (Imperial Censor), Palaphon Ankarien (Dean of the Lyceum) and Izora Highwind (Penumbral Watcher). Raficci Vicente Barossa and Veikko Bondforger won Conclave support for the Throne. Ylenwe was moved to Neutrality and Siakha to enmity. Sadogua agreed to move Damakan's Forge to Zenith, and the bargains with Prospero over Jarm and Skoura were accepted. The Shuttered Lantern was sent to Sarvos and the Silver Chalice to the Barrens. The interdiction of Curse of Gangrenous Flesh failed.

n.Druj: The Conclave sent the Silver Chalice to investigate Druj sites of experimentation with novel diseases in the Barrens, and it rewarded Caleb of the Cenotaph with an artefact ring for destroying the Druj Miasma pillars in Zenith.
n.Grendel: The Shuttered Lantern was tasked with sending agents to Sarvos to discover whether a Grendel espionage ring operates there and, where possible, to neutralise it.
n.The League: Shuttered Lantern agents will search the League territory of Sarvos for Grendel spy networks and other hidden threats to the Empire.
n.Thule: In accepting the ornate wyrmlings' offer, the Conclave nominated the Thule, and the items recovered are to be passed to Tyburn Weaver, Grandmaster of the Shuttered Lantern.
n.Urizen: The eternal Sadogua will move the remains of Damakan's Forge from Spiral to a site beside the Crucible in Zenith, bringing a unique boon to the Urizen territory.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Dima Vasilyevna Novosad of Varushka claimed the title of Master of the Koboldi.

t.Sarvos: Agents of the Shuttered Lantern will go to Sarvos to uncover any Grendel espionage ring or other enemy intelligence-gathering in the territory.
t.The Barrens: Members of the Silver Chalice will travel into the howling wilderness of the Barrens to investigate Druj disease experimentation and the Karass and Yerende septs, with particular interest in illnesses resembling the Reikos flux.
t.Zenith: Damakan's Forge is to be moved by Sadogua to a site beside the Crucible in Zenith, and Caleb of the Cenotaph was honoured for destroying the Druj Miasma pillars there.

385YE Summer Solstice Imperial elections.d: Senators were elected for Bastion, Karov, Miaren, Mitwold, Redoubt, Sarvos, Sermersuaq, the Barrens and Weirwater. The Senate appointed Jarrigk Orzel as Imperial Consul, ten generals and many other officials. In the Synod, Aspar became Cardinal of Wisdom with 253 votes, Melchior of Adina's Charge became Cardinal of Courage, and Tabris, Son of Armisael, won Bishop of the Navigators with 420 votes. Lenarius Ankarien became Imperial Inquisitor with 3 votes. Bourse seats such as the Damatian Cliffs went for up to 285 thrones. Eliza became Grandmaster of the Order of the Unfettered Mind, and Rhydian Iolaire became Knight-protector of Summer.

n.Dawn: Lady Eve Orzel was elected to represent Weirwater, one of Dawn's territories, in the Senate.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the page names no Druj, but the Barrens, then held by the Druj, had a senator elected, Aramis du Froste.
n.Highguard: Suvi Frostbrand was elected Senator for Bastion, Highguard's territory.
n.Navarr: Llewellyn Leafstalker was returned as Senator for Miaren, giving the Navarr territory its voice in the Senate.
n.The League: Uberto Alessandri di Caricomare vacino a Sarvos was elected Senator for Sarvos, the League city-territory.
n.The Marches: Sally was elected Senator for Mitwold, representing the Marcher territory in the Senate.
n.Urizen: Sejanus of the Scarlet Guard was elected Senator for Redoubt, Urizen's territory.
n.Varushka: Myshki Marishka Letuchaya was elected Senator for Karov, Varushka's territory.
n.Wintermark: Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason was elected Senator for Sermersuaq, Wintermark's territory.

t.Bastion: Bastion's Senate seat went to Suvi Frostbrand at this summit.
t.Karov: Karov elected Myshki Marishka Letuchaya as its senator.
t.Miaren: Miaren's senator for the season was Llewellyn Leafstalker.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold returned Sally as its senator.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt elected Sejanus of the Scarlet Guard as its senator.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos elected Uberto Alessandri di Caricomare vacino a Sarvos as its senator.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq's Senate seat went to Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason.
t.The Barrens: A senator for the Barrens, Aramis du Froste, was elected, even though the territory was held by the Druj at the time.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater elected Lady Eve Orzel as its senator.

385YE Summer Solstice Senate sessions.d: The treasury stood at 606 thrones and 6 crowns. Funds went to raise a Dawnish army (250 thrones), resupply the military (275), rebuild Kahraman's roads (70) and build mithril statues watching the Black Plateau. The Senate removed sanctions on the Iron Confederacy, armed the Dreamers of the Dark Forest against the Druj in Echofell, outlawed objects from the Semmerlak and recognised the sept of Karass as foreigners, which is under scrutiny. The Brilliant Star was relinquished. New titles included the Imperial Huntsmarshall, Speaker of the Magpies and Architect of the Crucible. Commissions and announcements produced sinecures, follies, a high path to Otkodov and spy networks in Mareave and the Forest of Ulnak.

n.Dawn: The Senate disbursed 250 thrones and amended the motion to raise a new Dawnish army, while a Challenger in Waiting congregation sinecure was built in Weirwater.
n.Druj: The Empire authorised arming the Dreamers of the Dark Forest to drive the Druj out of Echofell and built a spy network in the Forest of Ulnak to speed the destruction of the fear cult.
n.Grendel: An Imperial spy network was built in the Grendel territory of Mareave, and the Minister of Historical Research began researching that land's Urizen history.
n.Highguard: The Abbey of Reconciliation was commissioned in Necropolis and the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion, but the self-funded Physician's Legacy in Casinea failed.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Legion Engineer built the Open Hand of the Ancestors congregation sinecure in Solvihill, Skarsind, creating the Guide to the Lost, after the Golden Market of Aggido proved restricted to a wayleave bearer.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the nation is not named, though the senator for Bregasland, which it held, proposed the Speaker of the Magpies title.
n.Navarr: Stones from Blood, a planned mana ministry for the Navarr Vates Council, was withdrawn before a vote.
n.The Brass Coast: Kahraman received 70 thrones for its roads and Kamkrag forts and guards for its bourse seats, while the Parador of the Kindled Flame orphanage was built in Siroc, Madruga.
n.The League: The Garrison of the League sinecure was built in Hanuri, the Steel Rings of Sarvos became the Great Chains of Sarvos, and an appraisal was commissioned on how the League can help the Urizen in Spiral.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: senators for Mournwold, Mitwold and Upwold proposed a raid-defence appraisal and several appointments, but the nation itself is not named.
n.Urizen: Urizen gained the Architect of the Crucible and Oblivion Sentinel titles and the reconstructed Gardens of Pallas, while the Brilliant Star in Redoubt was allocated as a national seat and then relinquished.
n.Varushka: Varushka gained the Offices of the Iron Roads, the Tolvoli Slaughterhouse, an improved Orieb, a high path to Otkodov and the new Imperial Huntsmarshall title proposed by its senators.
n.Wintermark: The Artisans Guild's guildhouse was built near the Runeforge in Hahnmark and Tekkupala's Hives in Kallavesa, while Sermersuaq's amendments to the Liberty Pact passed.

t.Astolat: Its senator received 250 thrones to raise a Dawnish army, and also seconded the Kahraman roads funding.
t.Bastion: The Grand Inspiration of the Way folly was commissioned in Bastion, while its senator's Imperial Warcaster amendment was withdrawn.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar is not named in any motion this summit.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Speaker of the Magpies title and seconded Stones from Blood.
t.Casinea: The self-funded Physician's Legacy herb sinecure planned for Cantiarch's Hold failed, though Casinea's senator successfully proposed the Grand Inspiration of the Way.
t.Hahnmark: A guildhouse and sinecure for the Artisans Guild was built near Runegrott and the Runeforge.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed lifting sanctions on the Iron Confederacy, which passed, and seconded the failed Barrens appraisal.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the mithril sculptures, receiving 11 thrones 6 crowns, and seconded relinquishing the Brilliant Star.
t.Kahraman: 70 thrones went to rebuilding Kahraman's roads and the Kamkrag forts, and a Caravan Guards adventure was funded to protect its bourse seats from raids.
t.Kallavesa: Tekkupala's Hives, a drug-producing sinecure, was commissioned in Wittal with the help of Varushkan bees.
t.Karov: An Office of the Iron Roads was built in Delev, and Karov's senator proposed the Imperial Huntsmarshall title.
t.Karsk: An Office of the Iron Roads was built in Ivarsgard, and Karsk's senator successfully proposed fully improving the town of Orieb.
t.Madruga: The Parador of the Kindled Flame, an orphanage folly, was built in Siroc.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the withdrawn Stones from Blood and seconded the Speaker of the Magpies.
t.Miekarova: The Tolvoli Slaughterhouse was built to sate the dubik, and an Office of the Iron Roads was built in Essk.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Feni advisor election and seconded the Asavea ambassador election.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the withdrawn Gardens of Pallas motion and seconded the Liberty Pact amendments.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the raid-defence appraisal and seconded the Feni advisor election.
t.Necropolis: The Abbey of Reconciliation, a weirwood sinecure to help ex-slaves and refugees into the Way, was built in Necropolis.
t.Ossium: An Office of the Iron Roads was built in Lomaa, and Ossium's senator proposed arming the Dreamers of the Dark Forest.
t.Redoubt: The Brilliant Star bourse seat in Redoubt was made an Urizen national seat, then relinquished as an Imperial position by a ratified constitutional motion.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the failed Physician's Legacy and seconded the Semmerlak law.
t.Sarvos: The Steel Rings of Sarvos were renamed the Great Chains of Sarvos, though no funds were disbursed for the fortification.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Minister of Historical Research election and seconded the Kahraman guards.
t.Semmerholm: A new law made it a crime to own, take or sell any object from the depths of the Semmerlak.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Liberty Pact amendments and seconded the Urizen in Spiral appraisal.
t.Skarsind: The Open Hand of the Ancestors was built in Solvihill, but the Golden Market of Aggido in Gildenheim did not go ahead.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: its senator received 275 thrones for military resupply and seconded the Sarvos motion.
t.Temeschwar: The Garrison of the League was built in Hanuri, and the Keeper of the Tome of the Temeschwar-Otkodov Mana Exchange became an annual title.
t.The Barrens: Its senator's motion to recognise the sept of Karass as foreigners passed but is under scrutiny, while an appraisal on integrating local septs failed.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Auditor of Senatorial Accountability changes and seconded the Physician's Legacy.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Asavea ambassador election and seconded the Mareave spy network.
t.Volodmartz: An Office of the Iron Roads was built in Ruin, and Volodmartz's senator proposed the high path to Otkodov.
t.Weirwater: The Challenger in Waiting, a congregation sinecure holding a Synod vote, was built in Weirwater.
t.Zenith: The Gardens of Pallas were reconstructed in Proceris and a mithril statue was commissioned there, while Zenith's senator seconded lifting the Iron Confederacy sanctions.

r.Skarsind/Solvihill: The Open Hand of the Ancestors congregation was built in northern Solvihill, with its Guide to the Lost appointed by the Imperial Orc National Assembly.
r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: The Garrison of the League business sinecure was built in Hanuri, appointed annually by the League generals.
r.Zenith/Proceris: The Gardens of Pallas were reconstructed here, and a mithril statue for the Oblivion Sentinel was commissioned in southern Proceris.

385YE Summer Solstice Synod judgements.d: The General Assembly refused to remove the Doctrine of Human Destiny (539–1464). Enacted mandates committed Highguard, the Marches and the Brass Coast to fund the sacred city at Bastion, whose design the Nine chose. Urizeni in Spiral were urged to withhold the secrets of the Block and keep apart until a reckoning, and some spires will secede. Dawn turned inward after freeing the Barrens. Highborn and Varushkans armed Ossium's Dreamers. Highguard spread word of Urizen's veneration of Sulemaine. Claude Videre was vindicated as fit to be Empress, Aspar and Melchior became Cardinals, and priests were warned against the heralds of Cold Sun.

n.Dawn: Enacted mandates turn the Dawnish inward to enjoy the fruits of victory, restore exiles' estates in Dawnguard while new settlers hold back, and shift Dawn towards aiding the Barrens septs. Highguard pledged peerless kinship in the Barrens, and Dawnish knights were urged to fight the heralds of Cold Sun.
n.Druj: The Navarr assembly called on Navarri entering Sarangrave to hunt the Druj Het Sarra Grubfeast, former governor of Dawnguard. The Synod also welcomed Kaela's Gift, already used by captives of the Druj, being extended to those facing the vallorn.
n.Grendel: Priests searched for Grendel spies after an espionage ring was found in Necropolis, and the Seventh Wave can now root out such rings in Highborn lands for a year. Wildfyre was set a penance for urging trade with the Grendel. The Synod also debated the Apulian Orcs' former virtues of Audacity, Fidelity and Retribution.
n.Highguard: Highguard will pour 25 wains of white granite and 50 crowns a season into the sacred city at Bastion, leaving nothing for other projects. Its mandates also spread word of Urizen's veneration of Sulemaine, cost each Highborn mana site a crystal a season to hunt the Whisper Gallery, and arm the Dreamers of Ossium.
n.Imperial Orcs: An enacted mandate forged a Sunstorm sept identity, and the liberated orcs of Dubhtraig and Beoraidh named themselves the Sannite sept. Bloodcrow Rasp was vindicated, and the Imperial Orcs asked Varushka to let their Day magicians study the Palace of Orieb.
n.Jotun: The Freeborn raised a Jotun-style burial mound over the dead of Fort Braydon, earning grudging Jotun respect. Wintermark affirmed it will still give quarter to the Jotun, and Mourn orcs were urged to reject Jotun teachings on the Abyss.
n.Navarr: The Navarr assembly urged growth of Isaella's Dance and honoured Brocéliande's Brokers for regalia made for its generals. It warned of Anarchy around the Gardens of Glory but declined to tear them down, called for the hunt of Sarra Grubfeast, and backed engaging the heralds of Cold Sun.
n.The Brass Coast: Each Freeborn territory affected by an enacted mandate will donate 4 wains of white granite and 8 crowns a season to Bastion's sacred city. Freeborn corsairs were urged to break the Asavean blockade of Sumaah. The assembly also rejected Vengeance and endorsed the Zemress Festival and heritage names.
n.The League: The League assembly unanimously accepted it owes a reckoning to the Urizeni of Spiral, but Urizen's enacted mandates mean the Block is withheld and Spiral's taxation drops sharply. Separately, a loan lets the Sand Fishers finish their Holberg sawmills, and bishops were sent to guide the Apulians.
n.The Marches: Marcher mandates commit white granite and crowns to Bastion, set threshers hunting the Whisper Gallery at the cost of mana crystal, and welcome the Mournwold Orcs north. The assembly also exalted the miners of the Singing Caves and warned of Siakha's heralds hunting Mitwolders.
n.Thule: Wintermark endorsed its mediators trading in good faith with the Thule at the hall of Wreck in Otkodov. Highborn priests urged benefactors to bring trade and aid to the Varushkan regions ceded to the Thule.
n.Urizen: Enacted mandates see Spiral's Urizeni withhold the Block and keep apart from the League in enclaves, with some spires seceding. At home, Urizen rejected Purity and renounced veneration of Sulemaine, while Highguard spread word that will sour Highborn feeling towards Urizen.
n.Varushka: A greater-majority mandate sees Varushkans arm the Dreamers of Ossium, and their units may train them for a year. The assembly also called for a school for Ossium, honoured the completed Iron Roads, and sought access to Varkula's tomb and a pilgrimage to the Cave of Zoria.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark entered Iron Osric into the Book of Heroes and called for Pakaanan's Pass to be rebuilt. It endorsed mediators trading with the freed Thule at Wreck and Otkodov, affirmed giving quarter to the Jotun, and vindicated General Kindra Surefoot.

t.Bastion: The Nine chose Millward Cowley's design and Skywise Gralka's art for the sacred city at Bastion. Highguard, the Marches and the Brass Coast now fund it each season, and a Berechiah monument at his basilica was encouraged.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: a Vigilance call to seek out Grendel spies along the southern coast is linked to the territories around the Bay.
t.Bregasland: The Marcher assembly urged benevolence towards Bregaslanders turned against the Empire by Bushel Sykes, and castigated Sykes as a traitor. It also recognised House Greywater's service alongside the Strong Reeds.
t.Brocéliande: Highborn priests backed building the Greenwatch against the Brocéliande vallorn. Navarr honoured Brocéliande's Brokers for artefacts made as regalia for Navarr generals.
t.Holberg: League bishops endorsed memorial spaces in Holberg's walls, which are being raised. An enacted loan lets the Sand Fishers complete their sawmills in Holberg.
t.Kahraman: An enacted mandate raised a Jotun-style burial mound over the orcs who fell at Fort Braydon. The Freeborn also celebrated the rebuilding of Kahraman's roads and aspired to climb the Gilded Peak.
t.Karsk: Highborn priests urged virtuous benefactors to bring trade and aid to the ceded lands south of the mountains, which appear to include Karsk's Krevsaty.
t.Madruga: Vigilance priests warned of a patrician carrying the 'Endless Thirst'. This appears to relate to the desiccating blight consuming the Great Grasses of Madruga.
t.Miaren: The Synod rewarded Corwyn Heartsbane 10 thrones towards debts from commissioning the Hall of the Seven in Miaren. The Hall will let Navarr captains explore vallorn hearts.
t.Miekarova: Highborn priests urged benefactors to bring trade and aid to the ceded regions south of the mountains, apparently including Miechernya.
t.Mitwold: The Marcher assembly raised the hue and cry because Siakha's heralds have begun hunting Mitwolders, urging priests to anoint, consecrate and hallow.
t.Mournwold: The Marches exalted the Singing Caves miners who fought the Jotun raid, and backed research into the Ore Hills Rebellion. Mournwold Orcs were offered sanctuary and work in the north, and Zephaniah was rewarded for magic letting Mournwold's ghosts speak.
t.Necropolis: Highborn priests will accompany the Seventh Wave to urge Necropolis citizens to reveal what they told the Grendel spy ring. Varushka also sought access to check the seals on Empress Varkula's tomb.
t.Ossium: Highborn and Varushkan mandates arm the Dreamers of the Dark Forest, and Varushka called for a school for Ossium's new citizens. A dose of true liao was granted to consecrate a monument to Kethry, and Yevanshka was rewarded for bringing the Way to Ossium.
t.Otkodov: Wintermark endorsed virtuous mediators travelling to Otkodov and trading at Wreck to help feed the freed slaves and better understand the Thule.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Shattered Tower, a Highborn chapter from Reikos, opened itself to inquisition to disprove claims of eternal influence.
t.Sermersuaq: Wintermark called for Pakaanan's Pass, which linked Sermersuaq to Skarsind before the Jotun collapsed it, to be rebuilt.
t.Skarsind: Wintermark called for the rebuilding of Pakaanan's Pass into Skarsind. Skarsind's senator Bloodcrow Rasp was vindicated for building up the territory without Senate funds.
t.Spiral: Spiral's Urizeni will withhold the Block and live apart in enclaves, with some spires seceding. Construction needs mithril and taxation falls sharply, while the League and Urizen have each acknowledged that a reckoning is owed. Priests were urged to bring the Way to the Apulians and liao to the Wolves of War.
t.The Barrens: Dawnish exiles regain estates while new settlers hold back, and Dawn shifts towards aiding the septs. Highguard pledged kinship support, and Navarr and Dawn agreed to walk the trods created by the Dance of Navarr and Thorn.
t.The Semmerlak: The Varushkan assembly called the Semmerlak forbidden and urged its citizens to seek prosperity in other waters. The Senate has recently barred taking things from its depths.
t.Therunin: The Synod urged vigilance against Anarchy fed by liao from the Gardens of Glory in Therunin. The Vigilance assembly called for the gardens to be torn down, though the Navarr assembly rejected doing so.
t.Upwold: An enacted mandate sets Vigilant Upwolders hunting blasphemers and other threats, with a civil service report due at the Winter Solstice. Navarr were urged to visit Joshua Benson's tomb at Pickham.
t.Volodmartz: The Guardian of the Maze of Zoria plans a pilgrimage to the Cave of Zoria in Volodmartz to study the stone tablet from which the Staff of Zoria was believed taken.
t.Zenith: True liao consecrated the Crucible of Fate to Prosperity, drawing architects, crafters and merchants. Botanists at the Bleak Tower were encouraged to return to Zenith if the Gardens of Pallas are rebuilt.

r.Holberg/Holfried: Mentioned in passing: not named directly, though the page covers Holberg's walls and the Sand Fishers' sawmills in Holberg.
r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: A Jotun-style burial mound was raised over the orcs who fell at the Battle of Fort Braydon, not far from the battle site.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: Mentioned in passing: the unscalable Gilded Peak between Braydon's Jasse and Serra Briante was named as a Freeborn aspiration.
r.Karsk/Krevsaty: Krevsaty is among the regions ceded to the Thule to which Highborn priests urged benefactors to bring trade and aid.
r.Miekarova/Miechernya: Miechernya is among the regions ceded to the Thule to which Highborn priests urged benefactors to bring trade and aid.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Hap the Soft of the Golden Hoof Farm in the Green March was rewarded with one ring. He was praised for bridging Mournwold Orcs and Marchers.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: The Marcher assembly backed Jedediah Boon's research into the Ore Hills Rebellion of 326YE to reveal and perhaps honour its leaders.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: Mentioned in passing: notes suggest the Highborn call for aid to ceded lands might include Bonewood.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: Wintermark's assembly called for the pass, collapsed by the Jotun, to be rebuilt, which would restore the Krampus's home and ease army movement.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Exiles who fled the Barrens will regain their estates in Dawnguard, while Dawnish settlers refrain from settling beyond it. Navarr also called for the hunt of its former Druj governor, Sarra Grubfeast.
r.Volodmartz/Opascari: The bearer of the Staff of Zoria intends a pilgrimage to the Cave of Zoria in the Opascari Mountains to study its stone tablet.

385YE Summer Solstice interlude.d: Military units could join the Break the Vyig adventure or the new War of Whispers. The 350-throne Guerdon went to units supporting the Iron Helms, Citadel Guard, Bounders, Fist of the Mountains and Summer Storm. Dho'uala in the Semmerlak cut fleet production for Dawn, Varushka and Holberg. Tharim's Black Frost drained Dawnish mana sites and farms in return for knights against the Barrens. Highborn and Ambition-preaching League congregations gained liao and votes. Raiders hampered Kahraman's titles. The Mournwold, Necropolis, Navarr herb gardens and League businesses gained boons. Farm and forest diversification became free outside several contested territories. The Assembly of the Nine opened a contest to remake Bastion, and three rituals entered Imperial Lore.

n.Dawn: Dawnish fleets lost a rank of production to Dho'uala's Tithe, and the Black Frost cost every Dawnish mana site a crystal and every farm 36 rings. In return, Tharim's steel-bound knights would support any Dawnish army attacking the Barrens.
n.Druj: Tharim's steel-bound knights were pledged to support Dawnish armies attacking the Druj-held Barrens, where farms and forests were also excluded from free diversification.
n.Grendel: Grendel merchants traded eagerly with Highborn businesses in Necropolis under the Wildfyre mandate. Grendel-held Feroz was excluded from free diversification, and the Atalaya Harbour discount would last only while the Freeborn did not control Feroz.
n.Highguard: Highborn congregations gained extra liao, two Synod votes and a crown of income from the Birthplace of the Way. Every Highborn business suffered a rank penalty to fund Free Folk tutelage, Necropolis businesses gained 2 crowns from Grendel trade, and a contest opened to transform Bastion.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc military units could take part, for one more season, in the Break the Vyig adventure to destroy the criminal organisation.
n.Jotun: Jotun-held Bregasland and Liathaven were excluded from free farm and forest diversification. The page noted that Kahraman's troubles might become moot if the Jotun conquered Jade Range.
n.Navarr: Thanks to the Great Forest Orcs, Navarr with herb gardens in Therunin, Hercynia, Miaren and Brocéliande could upgrade them for one fewer wain of weirwood.
n.The Brass Coast: Raiders cut production at the Damatian Cliffs and the Great Mine of Briante and restricted two Kahraman ministries. Regrow the Land's Heart was cast in Madruga against the blight, and Madruga fleets cost one less wain to upgrade.
n.The League: The League assembly's mandate let units join the Break the Vyig adventure, and Ambition congregations run by League citizens gained extra liao and votes. League businesses became cheaper to upgrade, while Holberg fleets suffered under Dho'uala's Tithe.
n.The Marches: Mournwold characters could retrain their skills and Mournwold businesses earned an extra 36 rings, while Marcher farmers could build mana-producing monoliths without the usual diversification cost.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that no new rituals were added to Urizen lore during the Spring Equinox.
n.Varushka: Varushkan fleets lost a rank of production to Dho'uala's Tithe, and the Varushkan assembly's mandate let military units join the Break the Vyig adventure.

t.Bastion: The Assembly of the Nine opened a contest for a construction to turn Bastion into a beacon for pilgrims and supplant Timoj as the centre of the Way of Virtue.
t.Bregasland: Resources in Bregasland were excluded from the waived cost of diversifying farms and forests.
t.Brocéliande: Navarr herb gardens in Brocéliande could be upgraded for one fewer wain of weirwood, though the territory was excluded from free farm and forest diversification.
t.Feroz: Feroz was excluded from free diversification, and the Atalaya Harbour fleet discount depended on the Freeborn not controlling it.
t.Hercynia: Navarr herb gardens in Hercynia could be upgraded for one fewer wain of weirwood with Great Forest Orc help.
t.Holberg: Fleets based in Holberg lost a rank of production as Dho'uala haunted the Semmerlak.
t.Kahraman: Orc and human raiders cut the Damatian Cliffs' output by 7 wains and the Great Mine of Briante's by 6. The Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills and the Mistress of the Dust Parador lost access to the top two ranks of their ministries while Senate-commissioned roads and kamkrag were built.
t.Liathaven: Resources in Liathaven were excluded from the waived cost of diversifying farms and forests.
t.Madruga: Regrow the Land's Heart was cast in Madruga to contain the desiccating blight on the Great Grasses, and fleets there cost one less wain of weirwood to upgrade while Atalaya Harbour remained.
t.Miaren: Navarr herb gardens in Miaren could be upgraded for one fewer wain of weirwood with Great Forest Orc help.
t.Mournwold: Summer magic let characters with resources in the Mournwold change their skills, and every business there produced an extra 36 rings as its crafts and wares were in demand.
t.Necropolis: Visiting Grendel traders boosted every business in Necropolis by an additional 2 crowns each season.
t.Spiral: Resources in Spiral were excluded from the waived cost of diversifying farms and forests.
t.The Barrens: Tharim's steel-bound knights would aid any Dawnish army attacking the Barrens, and resources there were excluded from free diversification.
t.The Semmerlak: The sovereign Dho'uala rose in the Semmerlak, haunting fleets with eerie encounters and raising the prices of the Ivarsgard Docks and Harbourmaster of the Semmerlak ministries.
t.Therunin: Navarr herb gardens in Therunin could be upgraded for one fewer wain of weirwood with Great Forest Orc help.

r.Kahraman/Jade Range: The Dust Parador in Jade Range lost the top two ranks of its ministry because moving metal out of the mountains was too dangerous, a matter that might become moot if the Jotun conquered the region.

385YE Summer Solstice winds of fortune.d: With allies, Dawn shattered the Druj in the Barrens, and the Senate granted it dominion there. The Jotun quit Kahraman, leaving only champions, and withdrew from Bregasland into Liathaven and Hordalant. A blight continues to ravage Madruga's Great Grasses. The vyig were broken. Through Salt Lord Kaliact's treaty, Spiral passed to the League, leaving its Urizeni inhabitants in turmoil. The Crucible of Fate began transforming Zenith. Further entries covered Autumn magic and eternals, Varushkan dealings with dark powers and orcs, Wintermark judgements, Marcher affairs, Imperial Orc allies and the claim that Navarr and Thorn live within Brocéliande. The page also listed the Spring Sentinel Gate conjunction outcomes and trade conditions.

n.Dawn: With its allies, Dawn conquered the Barrens and was granted dominion by the Senate, a centuries-old dream achieved at great cost, though the fighting is not yet done. Stories of dark happenings also emerged in northern Dawn.
n.Druj: The Druj armies in the Barrens were shattered and routed at Dawnguard, and several warbands and heralds were killed in Spring conjunctions. At the Jagged Stream, however, the Druj drove off Imperial heroes and reclaimed the mithril.
n.Grendel: The Grendel still hold Feroz and the port of Oran remains closed to Imperial fleets. Their own seven virtues, apparently a legacy of ancient Urizen missionaries, raise questions for the Synod.
n.Highguard: The Highborn offered aid to the beleaguered Brass Coast and sent Jared of the Suns of Couros to support Varushkan contact with orcs. Their priests reach outward to the other nations even as the Seventh Wave makes an alarming discovery.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs completed an armoury for the Ethengraw and an ossuary-temple for the Illarawm and began a garden for the Yerende. Three entire septs are now on the verge of joining them, raising questions about who the Imperial Orcs now are.
n.Jotun: The Jotun left Kahraman without fighting, leaving only their champions, and made an orderly retreat from Bregasland into Liathaven and Hordalant without their usual promise to return. They suffered losses in Spring conjunctions, including the death of Jarl Iduna.
n.Navarr: The Navarr assembly proclaimed that the exemplars Navarr and Thorn still live at the heart of the Brocéliande vallorn and vowed to destroy it and release them. Navarr captives were also rescued in Liathaven.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn risk being squeezed between the Jotun to the east and the Grendel and Asavean-allied Governor Rahab to the west as the peace treaty nears its end. A desiccating blight continues to ravage Madruga.
n.The League: The League gained Spiral through the Kaliact treaty, and its egregores must decide whether its Apulian Orcs can become citizens. Its cities continue their year-long competition, and the vyig have been broken.
n.The Marches: Marchers face the aftermath of the Jotun and Fisher occupation of Bregasland and a phantasmal miner over the Mournwold. In Upwold, an inspirational tomb for Benson the Bellringer is being called for.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan traders and volhov were encouraged to make peaceful deals with orcs, including the Thule.
n.Urizen: The Crucible of Fate is slowly restoring Zenith, and the Gardens of Pallas may be rebuilt more splendidly than before. The Urizeni of Spiral are reeling from its transfer to the League, and the consecration of Sulemaine's tomb remains controversial.
n.Varushka: Varushka's assembly urged bargains with dark powers and peaceful contact with orcs, and the completed Iron Roads opened new trade between its vales. An appraisal also found ways to lift the Druj threat from Ossium.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's priests and stormcrows passed three contentious judgements, including one calling for a Varushkan senator to be interred in the Kallavesa marshes, which the Wintermark Assembly may now try to settle. The Net and Vine's Autumn enchantment spread across the Empire.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: those interested in the Bay of Catazar were listed among the audiences for the Rings and Crowns wind of fortune.
t.Bregasland: The Jotun withdrew and Mathilda Fisher's household retreated to Hordalant, leaving grudges between fenlanders over who sided with the Fishers, while Bushel Sykes continues to spread secessionist rhetoric.
t.Brocéliande: The Navarr assembly declared that Navarr and Thorn live on at the heart of this vallorn, holding it open to the trods. Research at the Great Library is expected to reveal a way to destroy it.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel still hold Feroz, part of the threat facing the Brass Coast from the west.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: a few groups of fleeing vyig were reported slinking through Ossium into the Forest of Ulnak.
t.Holberg: A mandate encouraging bravos to debate the sword scholars and study Emperor Frederick boosted the Scholars of the Sword Academy's stipend by a third. Vyig were also killed in Holberg and Misericorde's Blade recovered.
t.Hordalant: The retreating Jotun pulled back into Hordalant, and the Fishers withdrew to their holdings there.
t.Kahraman: The Jotun left without a fight but their champions remain. Imperial heroes were driven back at Braydon's Jasse, champion warbands raided neighbouring territories and servants of Hayaak reaved across the land.
t.Kallavesa: Forge the Wooden Fastness was cast in Wittal Grove, and a contentious Wintermark judgement called for a Varushkan senator to be interred in Kallavesa's marshes.
t.Liathaven: The Jotun retreating from Bregasland pulled back into Liathaven, where Imperial heroes rescued Navarr captives and killed Jarl Iduna.
t.Madruga: A blight ravages the Great Grasses, held back only by Spring magic that is slowly losing ground. The Dry Patricians survived the Silver Chalice's attempt to destroy them, and a shroud hangs over the territory.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: Axos anger over Imperial involvement in the failure of their joint venture with the Grendel into the Mountains of the Moon continues to penalise trade.
t.Mournwold: A phantasmal giant miner appears nightly over the Ore Hills, stirring the mine-owner enfranchisement movement and the Mournwold Orcs. Ghosts were laid to rest in Greensward.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis is listed among the territories over which a shroud hangs.
t.Ossium: An appraisal found opportunities to remove the under-threat status from Echofell and the Drownbark Forest. Forge the Wooden Fastness was cast in Echofell, and some fleeing vyig passed through the territory.
t.Sarangrave: Imperial heroes sprang an ambush on Ormthak's Path in the Bloodwater Marsh and killed a Druj warband.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: swift ships reportedly left Sarvos carrying suspiciously wealthy vyig passengers, and a shroud hangs over the territory.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun could return into Segura at any moment, and a shroud hangs over the territory.
t.Semmerholm: Heroes slew the Amaranthine Devourer, herald of Agramant, at Melusine's Field in Axmure.
t.Sermersuaq: In Spring conjunctions, the Ender of Virtue was defeated in Stark, the Jotun were stopped short of the Pride of Ikka's Tears, and Theodric Irontongue and the Walkers of the Wastes were killed.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Tamazi are noted as already settled in their new home in Skarsind.
t.Spiral: Spiral was regained in a single season through the Kaliact treaty and made a League territory, though whether its Apulian Orcs become citizens rests with the League egregores. Its Urizeni inhabitants are in turmoil.
t.Temeschwar: Heroes defeated the Grand Enchantrix and her Spites at Agnieszka's Grove in Metri.
t.The Barrens: The Druj were routed and the Barrens became Imperial under Dawnish dominion. Much work and further fighting remain, alongside numerous conjunction victories across the territory.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: more information about the disruption of the Semmerlak is promised in The Horror and the Wild wind of fortune.
t.Upwold: The Marcher assembly backed an inspirational tomb for Benson the Bellringer, whose legacy survives in Upwold's Pickham Monastery, and a conjunction to visit Benson's Orchard has appeared.
t.Zenith: The completed Crucible of Fate is slowly transforming Zenith, with new spires rising, and the destroyed Gardens of Pallas have been appraised for grander restoration. Dripping Echoes of the Fen were summoned in Proceris.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: Dripping Echoes of the Fen were summoned in the Grey Fens last season.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: At the Greywater Estates, Imperial heroes killed all the Jotun but recovered no letter.
r.Brocéliande/Terunael: Heroes who reached Terunael at the heart of Brocéliande found the exemplars Navarr and Thorn still living within the vallorn.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: Mentioned in passing: the Merchant Prince of Misericorde Market led the conjunction that recovered Misericorde's Blade in Utterlund.
r.Holberg/The Morass: Imperial heroes killed all the vyig at Drusilla's Farm.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: At Elsbeth's Well, Misericorde's Blade was recovered and the vyig slain.
r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: Heroes investigating the gathering of champions were driven back, after which champion warbands raided neighbouring territories.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: The Jotun were defeated on the Path of the Liscano family, and Venator, herald of Hayaak, was stopped on the Sylvan Track so that House Perigord could keep supplying Boar's Market.
r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: Forge the Wooden Fastness was cast in Wittal Grove last season.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Ring: At the Shattered Glade, the Navarr captives were rescued and Jarl Iduna was killed.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: The ghosts at the Overton Ruins were laid to rest.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: A phantasmal giant, shirtless miner appears above the Ore Hills every night, striking dramatic poses that mine owners and Mournwold Orcs each read as aimed at them.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Naomi of Virtue's Rest's appraisal found opportunities to remove the Drownbark Forest's under-threat status.
r.Ossium/Echofell: Echofell was appraised for removal of its under-threat status, and Forge the Wooden Fastness was cast there.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: On Ormthak's Path, the ambush was triggered and a Druj warband killed.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: The Amaranthine Devourer, herald of Agramant, was slain at Melusine's Field.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: At Nestori's Lament, the Ender of Virtue was defeated and its relic recovered and destroyed.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: The Jotun were stopped at Ymma's Howe before reaching the Pride of Ikka's Tears, and Theodric Irontongue and the Walkers of the Wastes were killed at Ardith's Rest.
r.Temeschwar/Metri: The Grand Enchantrix and her Spites were defeated at Agnieszka's Grove.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: At Spinner's Retreat, Venomclaw, herald of Arhallogen, was slain along with most of the Druj.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: The major conjunction to claim Dawnguard saw Serra Grubfeast's Druj routed and the Dawnish rebels succeed.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: Heroes recovered the relic of Adelmar at Hadrienne's Lament, claimed a stockpile at the Steadfast Pines and negotiated with the Vendarri on Greenstone Isle.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: At the Blooming Grove, tepel Zortog Ashtouch was killed and the list acquired.
r.The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth: Ramparts of Ashlar was cast on the Spires of Dusk, dead knights were given succour, the Gyre's Edge was recovered and the Druj were intercepted before they could attack the Rahvin.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: At Jagged Stream, the Druj drove off the Imperial heroes and reclaimed the mithril.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Dripping Echoes of the Fen were summoned in Proceris last season.

385YE Summer Solstice winds of war.d: In the east, Imperial armies worked to secure the Barrens despite Druj curses. In the west, the Empire advanced into Kahraman as the main western forces retreated, while Jotun and yegarra raided Madruga, Tassato, Sarvos and the Mournwold, and fighting raged around Fort Braydon. Wintermark and Skarsind warriors invaded Skallahn. Marcher armies and the Urizen-enchanted Granite Pillar were in Bregasland; the Jotun withdrew from the Dour Fens into Liathaven, and Mathilda Fisher returned to Hordalant, though Bushel Sykes remained stirring secessionism. The Wolves of War successfully claimed Spiral. Three possible Jotun battles were identified in Kahraman and Skallahn, alongside many conjunctions across the Empire.

n.Dawn: Dawnish forces (force weight 46) were offered conjunctions to protect the Harps of Astolat, investigate Surlac, challenge the Deadwood Knight in Weirwater and bring peace to the ghosts at the Shrine of Hope, while Dawnish armies could not take the Cautious Advance or Give Ground orders.
n.Druj: The Druj cast malign curses across the Barrens as Imperial armies tightened their grip, and faced conjunctions in the Barrens, Sarangrave and Ossium, though no major battle conjunctions involved them this season.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a conjunction in Grendel-held Feroz offered a meeting with emissaries of Siakha.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar marched across the Empire to Bregasland with Urizen magic, Highborn armies could no longer issue the Crusading Storm order, and Highborn forces had a force weight of 20 for the battles.
n.Imperial Orcs: Warriors from Skarsind joined Wintermark in crossing into Skallahn for the first invasion of the Jotun jarldoms, and the Imperial Orcs had a force weight of 5.
n.Jotun: The Jotun's main western forces retreated from Kahraman while their raiders struck across the west, their armies pulled back from the Dour Fens into Liathaven, and their own jarldom of Skallahn was invaded for the first time, with all three battle opportunities set against them.
n.Navarr: Navarr had a force weight of 52 for the battles and was offered a conjunction to protect the Pool of Silver Clouds in Miaren, with the Senator for Therunin given responsibility for a conjunction against the Druj in the Barrens.
n.The Brass Coast: Imperial forces advanced into Kahraman as Jotun and yegarra raided Madruga, Fort Braydon came under threat, and numerous Freeborn-led conjunctions arose in Madruga and Reinos; the Brass Coast's force weight was 19.
n.The League: The Wolves of War successfully claimed Spiral as agreed with the orcs there, while Tassato and Sarvos were raided and conjunctions targeted Magnus Ironarm and the last Temeschwari vyig; the League's force weight was 16.
n.The Marches: Some Marcher armies aided the Freeborn while others held Bregasland after Mathilda Fisher withdrew, though Bushel Sykes kept spreading secessionist ideas; the Mournwold was raided, and Marcher armies gained extra strength at home but could not Give Ground.
n.Urizen: Urizen magicians enchanted the Granite Pillar's march to Bregasland, Urizen armies gained bonuses in fighting between Zenith and Morrow, the Court of the White Fountain could not be reduced below 1,000 strength, and Urizen's force weight was 15.
n.Varushka: Varushka faced conjunctions to kill the last Varushkan vyig and the Druj in Ossium, could take the Hospitality of the Boyars order there, and generated fewer victory points when campaigning alongside the Brass Coast or Wintermark; its force weight was 11.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark warriors led the first invasion of the Jotun jarldoms in Skallahn, the nation brought the largest force weight of 60, and a conjunction sought to protect the Aviary of Ishal in Kallavesa.

t.Astolat: A conjunction was offered to protect the Harps of Astolat in Winterbourne.
t.Bregasland: Marcher armies and the Granite Pillar held Bregasland after the Jotun left the Dour Fens and Mathilda Fisher withdrew, though Bushel Sykes remained active and a conjunction offered a meeting with him.
t.Feroz: A conjunction at Azcara's Field in the Cazar Straits offered a meeting with emissaries of Siakha.
t.Hordalant: Mathilda Fisher, her supporters and household returned to their former domain in Hordalant after quitting Bregasland.
t.Kahraman: Imperial soldiers advanced into Kahraman as the main western forces retreated, with battle opportunities to block the passes out of Serra Damata and to stop Fort Braydon collapsing.
t.Kallavesa: A conjunction was offered to protect the Aviary of Ishal in Skymark.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: a conjunction against the Deadwood Knight took place in woods on Weirwater's border with Karov.
t.Liathaven: The Jotun armies pulled back into Liathaven after leaving the Dour Fens shortly after the Spring Equinox.
t.Madruga: Jotun and yegarra raids spread war into Madruga, prompting several conjunctions including stopping the Jotun at Torres and ending the Tassatan vyig at Calvos Sound.
t.Miaren: A conjunction was offered to protect the Pool of Silver Clouds in the Goldglades.
t.Miekarova: A conjunction was offered to kill the last of the Varushkan vyig at Srodkoja.
t.Mitwold: Any Imperial army could Billet in Mitwold, Marcher armies fighting there gained strength, and a conjunction was offered to deal with heralds on the Golden Downs.
t.Morrow: Highborn or Urizen armies defending Morrow against attacks from Zenith gained a bonus to defend territory but inflicted fewer casualties.
t.Mournwold: Jotun and yegarra raids spread into the Mournwold, a conjunction sought to stop Jarl Haakon at Southmoor, and Marcher armies fighting there gained extra strength.
t.Ossium: A conjunction was offered to kill the Druj in the Drownbark Forest, and Varushkan armies could take the Hospitality of the Boyars order here.
t.Redoubt: The Court of the White Fountain in Redoubt could not be reduced below 1,000 military strength.
t.Reinos: A conjunction was offered to recover the Overflowing Platter at Bastasor.
t.Sarangrave: A conjunction was offered to rescue Decius Frostpire from the Nesustak Forest.
t.Sarvos: Jotun and yegarra raids spread war into Sarvos.
t.Semmerholm: The Adamant Gate in Semmerholm could not be reduced below 1,000 military strength.
t.Skallahn: Wintermark and Skarsind warriors invaded Skallahn in the first assault on the Jotun jarldoms, with a battle opportunity against Blade Quencher's Hall and conjunctions at Iron Stand and Greenwall.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: warriors from Skarsind joined the crossing into Skallahn.
t.Spiral: The Wolves of War entered Spiral to claim it as agreed with the orcs there and succeeded despite the malignancy left by the Black Plateau's awakening.
t.Tassato: Jotun and yegarra raids spread into Tassato, and a conjunction was offered to slay Magnus Ironarm at Enterio.
t.Temeschwar: A conjunction was offered to kill the last of the Temeschwari vyig in Vardstein Vale.
t.The Barrens: Imperial armies worked to secure the Barrens despite Druj curses, with conjunctions against the Druj across Hope's Rest, the Untrod Groves and the Heart of Peytaht.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Senator for Therunin was given responsibility for a conjunction in the Barrens.
t.Upwold: Any Imperial army could Billet in Upwold, Marcher armies fighting there gained strength, and a conjunction offered a visit to Benson the Bellringer's orchard.
t.Weirwater: Conjunctions were offered to discover what was happening in Surlac and to challenge the Deadwood Knight in Wickmoor.
t.Zenith: Highborn or Urizen armies attacking Zenith from Morrow gained a bonus to territory captured but inflicted fewer casualties.

r.Astolat/Winterbourne: The High Bard of the Empire was named to organise protection of the Harps of Astolat at the Gardens of House Cadence.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: A small conjunction at the Ottery Fishing Docks offered a meeting with the secessionist Bushel Sykes.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: A conjunction at Azcara's Field offered the Archmage of Spring a meeting with emissaries of Siakha.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: A battle opportunity was identified to block the mountain passes out of Serra Damata against the Jotun.
r.Kallavesa/Skymark: A conjunction at Maiko's Copse sought to protect the Aviary of Ishal.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: A conjunction at Renewal Grove sought to end the Tassatan vyig and reclaim the documents.
r.Madruga/Torres: A conjunction at Fondre's Rest sought to stop the Jotun.
r.Miaren/Goldglades: A conjunction at the Verdant Grove sought to protect the Pool of Silver Clouds.
r.Miekarova/Srodkoja: A conjunction at Butterfly Holt sought to kill the last of the Varushkan vyig.
r.Mitwold/Golden Downs: A conjunction on the Long Road sought to deal with the heralds.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: A conjunction at Maggie's Croft sought to stop Jarl Haakon.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: A conjunction at Broken Clearing sought to kill the Druj.
r.Reinos/Bastasor: A conjunction at Beatriz's Field sought to recover the Overflowing Platter.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: A conjunction at the Thicket of Thorns sought to rescue Decius Frostpire.
r.Skallahn/Greenwall: A conjunction at Paegga's Rest sought to stop Jarl Asbjørn Dalgaard.
r.Skallahn/Iron Stand: A conjunction at Kevan's Holt sought to recover the shield of Blerung the Bright Lantern.
r.Tassato/Enterio: A conjunction at Duarte's Repose sought to slay Magnus Ironarm.
r.Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale: A conjunction in the Broken Wilds sought to kill the last of the Temeschwari vyig.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: A conjunction at the Silent Glade sought to stop the Druj.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: Conjunctions sought to rout the Druj and rescue Circe at Oakenclough and to bring peace to the ghosts at the Shrine of Hope.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: A conjunction at Garstang Thicket sought to stop Varag Soulflayer.
r.Upwold/Tower March: A conjunction offered a visit to the orchard of Benson the Bellringer.
r.Weirwater/Sandling: A small conjunction sought to find out what was going on in Surlac.
r.Weirwater/Wickmoor: A conjunction in woods on the border of Karov offered a chance to challenge the Deadwood Knight.

A glorious victory.d: Fayres, tourneys and mass ennoblements of yeofolk swept Dawn, and most Summer eternals were pleased, though the dethroned herald Hayaak raged. The Dawnish National Assembly was offered competing mandates: either turn towards prosperity at home or press the war against the remaining Druj. A second set of competing mandates would encourage settlement of the Barrens, urge caution, or support its factions instead. The Druj still held parts of the Barrens, the Karass and Vendarri remained hostile, the Montanians defiant, and the Rahvin had seized the Fangs. Most of the Barrens was unknown, so no regular commissions could be raised there for now. A Sentinel Gate conjunction would reach the Shrine of Hope.

n.Dawn: Dawn realised its centuries-old dream at the cost of the Hounds of Glory. Its National Assembly now faced competing choices over prosperity or war, and over settling the Barrens or holding back.
n.Druj: The Druj armies in the Barrens were shattered, though they still clung to the Heart of Peytaht and half of Murderdale. As they retreated they lashed out with curses, summoned defences and ancient trees.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: their custom of carrying torches on the Day of the Dead was cited as a model for the torchlit procession through the Sentinel Gate.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the rebellious Rahvin were noted as still willing to speak with the Imperial Orcs of the Winter Sun.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the liberation of Ossium was noted as an earlier step in the war against the Druj.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: their torchlit journey to the Kallavesa marshes was cited as an example for the Sentinel Gate conjunction.

t.Astolat: Astolat's people joined the nationwide jubilation, with fayres, tourneys and celebrations held in honour of the conquest.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's earlier torchlit journey to the Kallavesa marshes was cited as an example for this conjunction.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: its liberation from the Druj was cited alongside the freeing of the Barrens.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: named among the lands the Druj still held, which a war-focused Dawnish mandate might open new fronts against.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm celebrated the victory with fayres and tourneys. The ruined Towers of the Dawn that once kept the Druj out of it could now be rebuilt.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens was conquered and granted to Dawn, but it remained largely unknown, scarred by Druj pillage and home to hostile septs. No regular commissions could be raised there for now, and mandates on whether and how to settle it were on offer.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater shared in the elation across Dawn, hosting celebrations of the long-awaited conquest.

r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Mentioned in passing: not named directly, and covered only as part of the wider Barrens, much of which remained unknown to the Empire.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Dawnguard bore the scars of occupation, with the Towers of the Dawn ruined and Drycastle pillaged. The Empire could rebuild the towers (60 white granite, 15 thrones, nine months) or restore Drycastle as a sinecure creating a Knight of Dawnguard and a Reeve of Drycastle.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: The Heart of Peytaht remained under Druj control, and Imperial armies were urged to remove this last vestige of their authority.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: Dozens of ghosts were converging on the Shrine of Hope, said to hold the grave of Ser Guineve. A Sentinel Gate conjunction offered all of Dawn the chance to visit and create a permanent aura there.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Half of Murderdale was still held by the Druj, who continued to strike at the Empire from what remained to them.

A lost king.d: The Black Forge in Gildermark began slowly arming the Ethengraw, who also bought paper to rebuild their Epic. The Senate could now raise a new Imperial Orc army from the Ethengraw for 200 mithril and 50 thrones over a year, but it must bear a Proud name and must not be called a third legion. The Illarawm Ossuary in Southpine opened, and its mystagogues began collecting ancestors' names, stories and bones across Skarsind. The Yerende garden is paid for and expected by the Equinox. Following Archmage Gralka's judgement, the Assembly could adopt the name Sunstorm Sept by mandate. Apulian, Mournwold and Great Forest orcs may join other nations.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: they are named as the former overlords who broke the Ethengraw, destroyed every copy of their Epic and scattered the Illarawm's ancestral bones.
n.Imperial Orcs: The nation stands to gain the Ethengraw, Illarawm and Yerende as septs at the Autumn Equinox. It may also raise a new Ethengraw army and was invited to adopt the name Sunstorm Sept for the descendants of Thrace.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: there are signs that some Great Forest Orcs might one day join the Navarr.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Apulian orcs look set to join the League, and Tassato is used as a comparison of scale.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Mournwold orcs have been looking to join the Marchers for years.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Bone Temple's modest exterior is likened to a tiny Urizen temple.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Ossium, now Varushkan-held, is where the Ethengraw once ruled and which the three septs left together.

t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: its orcs are noted as having long sought to join the Marchers.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Ethengraw recall once ruling all of Ossium, and the three septs left it together.
t.Skarsind: The Black Forge and the Illarawm Ossuary were completed here, the Yerende garden is under way, and Illarawm mystagogues toured local villages gathering ancestors' names, stories and bones.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: comparing the Ossuary with the Black Forge is likened to comparing Tassato with a hamlet.

r.Skarsind/Gildermark: The Black Forge was completed here, its dozen forges running night and day to arm the Ethengraw, who also bought paper and blank books traded from Gildermark.
r.Skarsind/Southpine: The Illarawm Ossuary, a vast bone-lined crypt beneath a modest temple, was completed here, and its mystagogues set out into southern Skarsind to record ancestors and collect bones.

A tide in the affairs.d: Welcomed at Ballaghadruh by Kaliact's garrison commander Rhababahrúns, the Wolves followed Kaliact's proposed itinerary through Ossuary, Ankra, Cinion, Ateri, Screed, Apstrus and finally Apulus. Fighting was limited to scattered loyalist orcs and miasma-maddened wretches in Screed, but the Black Plateau drove many soldiers to desert. Kaliact had used forged orders to send the Black Eels and Brine Turtles to Mareave, then used the procession to buy time to crush loyalists in the City of Nets. By season's end Spiral was part of the Empire, but Kaliact's supporters held control only narrowly, and Paymaster Muireall led a peaceful holdout camp in southern Apstrus.

n.Grendel: Spiral's Grendel split between Kaliact's conspirators, bewildered bystanders and loyalists to Dubhtraig, who fought and lost at Apulian's docks and palace. Two Grendel armies were sent to Mareave by forged orders.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Hercynian Navarr scouts, skilled at moving unseen through Spiral's broken terrain, accompanied the Wolves of War.
n.The League: The League's Wolves of War brought Spiral into the Empire as a new League territory, losing soldiers mainly to desertion under the Black Plateau's influence and to a few skirmishes.
n.Urizen: Urizeni met in Ankra and Cinion gave the Wolves a mixed welcome, some feeling betrayed and some preparing to leave Spiral for Redoubt, Morrow or Zenith.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay is not named; the only maritime element is the loyalists' attempt to seize or burn ships at Apulian's docks.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Hercynian Navarr scouts were recruited to help the Wolves of War move through Spiral.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the Black Eels and Brine Turtles left Spiral for Mareave on forged orders, and Kaliact had expected Paymaster Muireall to retreat there.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: some Urizeni in Spiral prepared to leave for Morrow.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: Paymaster Muireall was almost ruined by a disastrous venture into the Mountains of the Moon.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: some Urizeni in Spiral prepared to leave for Redoubt.
t.Spiral: Spiral was secured by the Wolves of War and became a League territory of the Empire, though Kaliact's hold on its orcs remained fragile and the Black Plateau's miasma persisted.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: some Urizeni in Spiral were even preparing to leave for Zenith.

r.Spiral/Ankra: In Ankra the Wolves met their first Urizeni, whose welcome was mixed and some of whom were preparing to leave Spiral.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: Apstrus, site of the Battle of Solen's Doubt, saw a little more resistance, and Paymaster Muireall established a non-violent holdout camp of anti-Imperial orcs on its southern borders.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Kaliact's supporters won a bloody fight against loyalists in the City of Nets, especially at the docks and palace, leaving Apulian tense and only narrowly under her control.
r.Spiral/Ateri: At Ateri Rhababahrúns returned to Ballaghadruh and was replaced as escort by Captain Chevahn of Kaliact's guard and two Circle of Black Sand magicians.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Urizeni in Cinion greeted the Wolves with barely concealed anger and a sense of betrayal, and some made ready to leave.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: At the Legacy mithril mine Kaliact's orcs had seized control after fighting off the Lamhaich family, whose Overseer Seàrlas Lamhaich fled, and here the Wolves first felt the Black Plateau's miasma again.
r.Spiral/Screed: Screed, where the Black Plateau is strongest, was secured after fighting miasma-maddened killers that cost a score or so of soldiers, and Oblivion's Edge sentinels warned of increased activity near the Plateau.

Battle cries.d: Captains of the League, Varushka and the Imperial Orcs crushed the vyig, ending the bite trade but leaving a vacuum of disorganised crime. Three groups remained: Uncle Tassato carrying a stolen copy of the Regario Dossier, Miekarovan vyig with a mysterious patron bound for the Butterfly Holt, and Aunt Alina's gang in Vardstein Vale after a bloody raid on the Assayer's Guild. Magistrates confiscated vyig-linked businesses in Tassato, Sarvos and Karov. The Silver Rook Carta sought a League Assembly mandate to publish the names of the vyig-hunters. A Lantern Wolf office could be built in one of the four League cities before the end of Winter 385YE.

n.Druj: Evidence marked bite as a Druj product, and the vyig who escaped fled into the Mallum, where they almost certainly learned how little the Druj can be trusted.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the fleeing Tassatan vyig were preparing a final leg of their journey to Grendel-held Feroz.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Imperial Orc captains were among those who directly opposed and helped break the vyig.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun were expected simply to enslave any Varushkan vyig who reached their border.
n.The Brass Coast: The Tassatan vyig were reportedly hiding in the Renewal Grove in Brass Coast-held Madruga, so the fight to recover the stolen Regario Dossier would take place on Freeborn land.
n.The League: The League saw its ancient criminal syndicate destroyed, gained confiscated businesses and fee-free business opportunities in Tassato and Sarvos, and was offered a mandate to honour the vyig-hunters and the chance to create a Lantern Wolf to guard against a new syndicate.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule were considered unlikely to offer the fleeing Varushkan vyig shelter.
n.Varushka: Varushka's vyig were all but destroyed, with Orel the Bondbreaker slain, though the last Miekarovan band threatened the Butterfly Holt and a vyig-owned mine and business in Karov were seized for Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti to dispose of.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Feroz was the intended final destination of Uncle Tassato's escape.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: a few groups of vyig were reported slinking through Ossium into the Forest of Ulnak.
t.Holberg: The garrison of the Walls of Holberg supported the city against the vyig, and Holberg was one of the cities where a Lantern Wolf office could be built, implying a pragmatic, ingenious investigator.
t.Karov: Magistrates recovered a vyig-owned mine and business in Karov, both legitimate enterprises, whose deeds were given to Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti to deal with at the summit.
t.Madruga: The last Tassatan vyig were believed to be hiding in Madruga's Renewal Grove, located with help from a Mestran herb seller's sighting in the markets of Calvos, awaiting interception by the Custodian of the Regario Dossier.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova saw running skirmishes and the death of vyig leader Orel the Bondbreaker near the vale of Olodny, but his surviving band regrouped in the woods to strike at the Butterfly Holt.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: a few groups of vyig were reported slipping through Ossium into the Forest of Ulnak.
t.Sarvos: Swift ships left Sarvos carrying suspiciously wealthy passengers, a vyig-linked business there was confiscated and its deed given to Irada von Temeschwar, and the city was a possible site for an elegant, sophisticated Lantern Wolf's office.
t.Tassato: Tassato suffered running skirmishes and the burning of the vyig lair at the Jarmish Lodge; two confiscated businesses passed to Irada von Temeschwar, League citizens could take new businesses there without the usual fee, and it was a possible site for a diplomatic Lantern Wolf.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar endured skirmishes and a bloody vyig heist on the Assayer's Guild that killed and captured clerks and angered House de Courcey, and it was a possible site for a ruthless, hard-nosed Lantern Wolf.

r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: A Sentinel Gate conjunction offered the chance to intercept Uncle Tassato's band at the Renewal Grove in Calvos Sound and recover the stolen Regario Dossier before they left for Feroz.
r.Miekarova/Srodkoja: The last Miekarovan vyig were set to attack the Butterfly Holt in southern Srodkoja, threatening significant damage that would cut its production of iridescent gloaming unless the Gloaming Sentinel's allies intercepted them.
r.Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale: Aunt Alina's gang held an abandoned fort in the Broken Wilds of Vardstein Vale, having slaughtered the Green Torch bravos, and the Custodian of the Assayer's Guild was charged with ending them and taking her head for House de Courcey.

Chords.d: The Apulian Orcs endorse Ambition, Prosperity and Vigilance, but also prize audacity, cunning, fidelity and retribution, viewing all virtues as pathways to power. Their questioners petitioned the Synod to rule on each quality before anyone fell foul of the law. The General Assembly could deem a quality a noble ideal like honesty or glory, condemn it as a malign spiritual force, or, with a doctrinal change, name it an eighth Virtue. Any Virtue assembly could instead claim one as an expression of its Virtue. Retribution in particular resembles the forbidden aura of Vengeance. The Apulians accept they may need to compromise, and Graime the Questioner was expected at Anvil to answer priests' questions.

n.Grendel: The Grendel orcs who defected in Spiral brought their own creed, built on the pursuit of power and four virtues outside Imperial doctrine, and now await the Synod's verdict on which they may keep preaching.
n.The League: The League's egregores Harlequin and Innamorata were weighing whether to accept the Apulian Orcs as citizens, while the Synod's rulings would decide which of the orcs' ideals might spread through the League.

t.Spiral: Spiral's Apulian Orcs, now part of the Empire after the territory passed to the Wolves of War, were asking the Synod to rule on their beliefs, so the outcome would shape how their questioners may preach there.

Concord and accord.d: Four candidates stood in the latest Throne election (Bohemond De Rondell, Chiara i Zayden i Riqueza, Sir Claude Vyse Videre and Veikko Bondforger), but none won the required two-thirds. Æsa Sigeling's declaration met near-universal agreement. Magicians will now assume a Throne lacks Conclave support unless it has been explicitly given beforehand. The Conclave can approve any number of candidates, prefer a single one, or denounce candidates, and declarations passed after an appointment have no effect. A minority urges the Conclave to step back, which would weaken political Concords and the Imperial Magus for a year. Others suggest magicians stand as candidates or lobby their senators instead.

n.The League: Mentioned in passing: an Imperial magician wistfully compares his coven's evening to the wine-and-cake salons held in Holberg.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's salons are held up in the fiction as the model of a refined evening of political discourse.

Construct Abbey of Reconciliation.d: Proposed by the senator for Necropolis and seconded by Bastion, the motion created the Abbey of Reconciliation, overseen by the Abbess of Reconciliation. The Abbess is charged with supporting ex-slaves and refugees, bringing them into the Way, and giving them the opportunity to work and recover in the Empire. The title is elected by the Highborn National Assembly and revocable by the Highborn, General and Assembly of the Nine. Construction cost 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns in labour on top of standard costs, and took three months. Sister Rosa, Fintan Nighthaven and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov supplied the funds and weirwood. With the abbey complete, the first Abbess was to be appointed at the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

n.Highguard: Highguard gained a new national title, the Abbess of Reconciliation, elected by the Highborn National Assembly and charged with caring for ex-slaves and refugees and bringing them into the Way.

t.Necropolis: The Abbey of Reconciliation was built in Necropolis as a 10 weirwood sinecure, making the territory a centre for aiding ex-slaves and refugees within the Network of the Proffered Hand.

Construct Challenger in Waiting.d: Announced in Summer 385YE under an Imperial Wayleave, the Challenger in Waiting is a sinecure granting liao and a vote in the Synod, with a congregation based in Weirwater. The title is appointed by the Dawnish National Assembly, which expects the holder to appoint tourneys, and like the High Bard it may be held only once in a lifetime; regalia is to be provided. Construction cost 10 wains of white granite, 20 crowns in labour and standard costs, taking three months. Valentin Ivarovich Orzel supplied 2 thrones 4 crowns and the granite after the Summer Solstice. The first holder was elected at the Autumn Equinox 385YE, though the announcement remained subject to further scrutiny.

n.Dawn: Dawn's National Assembly gained a new once-per-lifetime title to appoint, its holder expected to call tourneys and given a vote in the Synod, with the first Challenger in Waiting elected at the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

t.Weirwater: The Challenger in Waiting was built in Weirwater, where its holder's congregation is based, using 10 wains of white granite.

Construct Garrison of the League.d: Elsha Bertolf, Chair of the Wolf, announced the commission of the Garrison of the League, a business sinecure in Hanuri, Temeschwar, to be appointed annually by League Generals. On top of standard costs, it required 10 wains of white granite, 20 crowns in labour and three months to build. Erikas Van Temeshwar funded it: 2 thrones, 4 crowns and 4 wains of white granite after the Summer Solstice 385YE, then the remaining 6 wains of white granite after the Winter Solstice 385YE. With construction complete, the position of Quartermaster of the Hanuri Garrison was due to be elected for the first time at the Spring Equinox 386YE.

n.The League: The League gained a new sinecure whose holder is chosen annually by its generals. A League citizen, Erikas Van Temeshwar, supplied the money and white granite needed to complete it.

t.Temeschwar: The League-held territory of Temeschwar is home to the new Garrison of the League, a business sinecure built with white granite supplied by Erikas Van Temeshwar.

r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: Hanuri is the site of the completed Garrison of the League, whose Quartermaster of the Hanuri Garrison was to be chosen for the first time at the Spring Equinox 386YE.

Construct Grand Inspiration of the Way.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Casinea and seconded by the senator for Temeschwar. It needed 951 wains of white granite, 49 wains of mithril and 2230 crowns in labour, and three years to build. Construction began after a suitably inspiring design was chosen at the Summer Solstice 385YE. Mandates brought seasonal contributions from the citizens of the Marches, the Brass Coast, Highguard, Wintermark, Navarr, the League and Dawn. Many individuals also donated over the following years. Highguard's support continues under the Benefactors Council. In 388YE the design was amended to add seven great bells, gardens for the Voices of Virtue and a choristers' balcony.

n.Dawn: Through a mandate enacted by Darian Numbers at the Winter Solstice 385YE, Dawn's citizens gave 16 wains of white granite and 32 crowns each season until the Winter Solstice 386YE.
n.Highguard: The edifice rises in Highguard's territory of Bastion. Its citizens have supported it since Eli of the Cenotaph's mandate, and they now give 12 wains of white granite and 36 crowns each season under the Benefactors Council's direction until it is completed.
n.Navarr: After Fintan Nighthaven's mandate at the Autumn Equinox 385YE, Navarr's citizens contributed until the Autumn Equinox 386YE. Their seasonal share fell from 12 wains of white granite and 24 crowns to 8 wains and 16 crowns because Navarr did not control Therunin.
n.The Brass Coast: After Sufyan i Zuhri i Erigo's mandate at the Summer Solstice 385YE, Brass Coast citizens contributed until the Summer Solstice 386YE. Their share fell from 12 wains of white granite and 24 crowns to 8 wains and 16 crowns because the Brass Coast did not control Madruga.
n.Wintermark: Through Eldrid Vestardottir's mandate at the Autumn Equinox 385YE, Wintermark's citizens gave 12 wains of white granite and 24 crowns each season until the Autumn Equinox 386YE.

t.Bastion: Bastion is the site of the Grand Inspiration of the Way, a temple-city whose construction began after its design was chosen in Summer 385YE. Its design was later enlarged with great bells, gardens for the Voices of Virtue and a choristers' balcony.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the Brass Coast's contribution to the project was reduced because the nation did not control Madruga.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Navarr's contribution to the project was reduced because the nation did not control Therunin.

Construct Guildhouse of the Artisans.d: Proposed by the senator for Hahnmark and seconded by Semmerholm, the motion created a guildhouse with a sinecure producing materials for artisans of the guild. The title of Guildmaster of the Artisans is appointed with tenure by the Senate, with the expectation that the guild will present its own chosen candidate. The motion credited the guild's ambition, prosperity and hard work with funding the work, and asked that any additional funds make the guildhouse grander and the envy of foreign nations. After the Summer Solstice, Xanthius Storm's End provided 8 wains of mithril, 4 thrones and 8 wains of white granite. Once complete, the guildhouse will create the Imperial title of Guildmaster of the Artisans.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gains an Imperial guildhouse for the Artisans Guild beside its own Runegrott and Runeforge, proposed by the senator for Hahnmark, which will give the nation's artisans a recognised sodality, a Guildmaster and a supply of materials.

t.Hahnmark: The guildhouse is to be built in Hahnmark, close to Runegrott and the Runeforge, and the territory's senator proposed the motion.

Construct High Path to Otkodov.d: Proposed by the senator for Volodmartz and seconded by Karsk, the motion commissioned the high path described in the Pride and Prejudice Wind of Fortune. It required 8 wains of white granite, 2 thrones in labour costs and three months to build. After the Summer Solstice, Kostjya supplied the granite, while Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov contributed money towards the labour. Once the path was completed, the resulting ministry allowed the custodian of the Gift of the Dwindling Star to trade food to the Thule for additional rings of ilium.

n.Thule: The Thule became the Empire's trading partner through the new ministry, receiving food from the custodian of the Gift of the Dwindling Star in exchange for additional rings of ilium.

t.Otkodov: A new high path was cut through the mountains to Thule-held Otkodov, creating a route for exchanging Imperial food for ilium.

Construct Mithril Sculptures.d: Proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by Redoubt's, the motion took up the opportunity offered by the Wind of Fortune 'The fate of the many'. It was recorded as passed at 11 thrones and 6 crowns. The sculptures needed 10 wains of mithril, 20 crowns in labour and three months to build. Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg supplied the mithril and 2 thrones 4 crowns after the Summer Solstice. Once completed, the folly allowed Vale of Shadows to shield Urizen personal resources in Spiral from foreign-nation penalties, and for the next year let that ritual be made permanent for a third of the usual ilium. The Urizen generals were first to elect an Oblivion Sentinel at the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

n.The League: Holberg's senator proposed the motion and Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg supplied the mithril and labour money that let the folly be completed.
n.Urizen: Urizen gained two mithril statues in its lands and a new national title, the Oblivion Sentinel, elected by its generals to guard against threats from the Black Plateau. Its citizens' personal resources in Spiral could also be shielded by Vale of Shadows.

t.Redoubt: One of the two mithril statues was built in Redoubt, whose senator seconded the motion.
t.Spiral: The completed folly allowed Vale of Shadows to shroud Urizen personal resources in Spiral from foreign-nation penalties, with the option to make that ritual permanent at reduced cost for a year.
t.Zenith: One of the two mithril statues was raised in Zenith, part of the folly tied to watching over the Black Plateau.

r.Redoubt/Optarion: A mithril statue was commissioned for the peaks of Optarion as one half of the folly.
r.Zenith/Proceris: A mithril statue was commissioned for southern Proceris as one half of the folly.

Construct Offices of the Iron Roads.d: Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, Master of the Koboldi, announced the commission under the Deep forests and dark hills wind of fortune. The offices were to be built in Ivarsgard (Karsk), Delev (Karov), Lomaa (Ossium), Essk (Miekarova) and Ruin (Volodmartz), at a cost of 30 wains of white granite, 30 wains of mithril and 15 thrones, taking six months. Borys Vardovich Straskovich supplied nearly all the materials and most of the money, with smaller contributions from Triska Markova, Kostjya and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov.
