The offices were completed, and the Boyar of the Iron Roads was to be appointed for a limited term by Tally of the Votes, first at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

n.Varushka: Varushka gained the Offices of the Iron Roads across five of its territories and a new national title, the Boyar of the Iron Roads, chosen by the Tally of the Votes. The work was funded largely by the Varushkan Borys Vardovich Straskovich.

t.Karov: One of the Offices of the Iron Roads was built at Delev in Karov.
t.Karsk: One of the Offices of the Iron Roads was built at Ivarsgard in Karsk.
t.Miekarova: One of the Offices of the Iron Roads was built at Essk in Miekarova.
t.Ossium: One of the Offices of the Iron Roads was built at Lomaa in Ossium.
t.Volodmartz: One of the Offices of the Iron Roads was built at Ruin in Volodmartz.

Construct Open Hand of the Ancestors.d: The project required 10 wains of white granite, 20 crowns in labour and three months to build. After the Summer Solstice the granite was supplied by several donors: Tut, Redhand Gezzar and Frith gave two wains each, and Nirak, Rok, Vrak and Protectorate Thenrik gave one wain each. Tut also provided 2 thrones and 2 crowns, and Rhys Nighthaven and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov gave a crown each. The work was completed. The Imperial Orcs National Assembly would make the first appointment to the new title of Guide to the Lost at the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs gained a new national title, Guide to the Lost, tied to the Open Hand of the Ancestors. Their National Assembly would first appoint it at the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind, held by the Imperial Orcs, became the site of the Open Hand of the Ancestors, a new congregation sinecure built with ten wains of white granite.

r.Skarsind/Solvihill: The Open Hand of the Ancestors congregation was built in the north of Solvihill.

Construct Parador of the Kindled Flame.d: The folly was announced by Laughlan, Master of the Rings, at a cost of 27 wains of white granite and 54 crowns in labour, with three months needed to construct it. After the Summer Solstice, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar provided 5 thrones, 3 crowns and all 27 wains of white granite, Triska Markova gave 1 throne, Sagua i'Ezmara 2 crowns and Bakar i Riqueza 1 crown. The page records no outcome, so whether the Parador was completed is not stated.

n.The Brass Coast: The planned Parador would give orphaned children of the Brass Coast a home in which hakima and kohan teach them the nation's traditions, and Brass Coast figures such as Sagua i'Ezmara and Bakar i Riqueza contributed coin towards it.

t.Madruga: The orphanage folly was to be raised in Siroc, Madruga, with all 27 wains of white granite pledged towards its construction, though no completion is recorded.

Construct Spy Network in Forest of Ulnak.d: Bernard Dugdale, Imperial Spymaster, announced a spy network in the Druj-held Forest of Ulnak in the Mallum, framing it as serving Imperial security, stability and victory against the "vile fear cult formerly known as the Druj". The project required 10 wains of weirwood, 20 crowns in labour and three months to build. Contributions arrived after the Summer Solstice from Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad, Triska Markova, Nathair Autumngale and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov, and after the Autumn Equinox Dugdale himself supplied nine wains of weirwood, with further crowns from Laughlan Vi Temeschwar and Ivana Petara Vodjavic. Once complete, military units could support the network to uncover information about the Forest of Ulnak.

n.Druj: The Druj are the explicit target, with the Spymaster declaring the network a means to speed the destruction of their "fear cult" by gathering intelligence on their lands.

t.Forest of Ulnak: The spy network was to be built to target the Druj-held Forest of Ulnak, letting Imperial military units uncover information about the territory once it was completed.

Construct Spy Network in Mareave.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Zenith and seconded by the senator for Upwold. It authorised an Imperial spy network in Mareave, then held by the Grendel. The cost was 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns in labour, plus standard costs, with three months to construct. After the Summer Solstice 385YE, Ematius 'Icebreaker' Ankarien provided 2 thrones, 4 crowns and the 10 wains of weirwood. Once complete, Imperial military units will be able to support the network to uncover information about the territory south of Spiral.

n.Grendel: The Empire is building a spy network inside Grendel-held Mareave, which will let Imperial armies gather intelligence on Grendel lands south of Spiral.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the network's purpose is described as gathering information about the territory south of the League's Spiral.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar is not named on the page, and the motion concerns only Mareave.
t.Mareave: An Imperial spy network is to be built in Grendel-held Mareave, funded by the Archmage of Winter and due for completion after three months of construction.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: League-held Spiral is used as the reference point, with the network watching the territory to its south.

Construct Tekupala's Hives.d: Proposed by the senator for Kallavesa and seconded by Hahnmark, the motion acted on the 'Thousands or more' Wind of Fortune. It created a sinecure producing unique drugs in Wittal, built with the permission of the Keeper of the Bones Hives of Varushka, whose bees would build the hives of Kallavesa. Construction required 15 wains of weirwood, 30 crowns in labour costs and three months. After the Summer Solstice, Kal provided 3 thrones 6 crowns and the 15 wains of weirwood. With the work complete, the sinecure is held by the Tender of Tekupala's Hives, a Wintermark national title appointed annually each Autumn Equinox by the Wintermark senators.

n.Varushka: The Varushkan Keeper of the Bones Hives gave permission for the sinecure, and their bees were to build the new hives in Kallavesa.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark gained a new national title, the Tender of Tekupala's Hives, appointed each Autumn Equinox by its senators to hold the drug-producing sinecure.

t.Kallavesa: Tekupala's Hives were built in Wittal, Kallavesa, with Kal providing the money and 15 wains of weirwood needed to complete them.

Construct Tolvoli Slaughterhouse.d: Proposed by the senator for Miekarova and seconded by Volodmartz, the motion was described as a limited-time, fully self-funded opportunity. The slaughterhouse required 12 wains of weirwood, 3 thrones in labour and three months to construct. After the Summer Solstice, Misha Klubnika Alexandrovich Petrov provided 2 thrones, 3 crowns and all 12 wains of weirwood, Kostjya gave 4 crowns and Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn gave 1 crown. With the work completed, the Varushkan national title of Tolvoli Butcher is appointed each Autumn Equinox by Tally of the Votes.

n.Varushka: Varushkan citizens funded the slaughterhouse through private donations, and the nation gained a new national title, the Tolvoli Butcher, appointed annually at the Autumn Equinox by Tally of the Votes.

t.Miekarova: The Tolvoli Slaughterhouse was built in Miekarova as a ministry to feed and placate the territory's dubik.

Culling the threat.d: Naomi offered several routes. Invading the Forest of Ulnak would permanently end the threat to any Ossium region no longer bordering Druj land. Echofell could be secured by commissioning a new Tower of the Manticore before the end of the Autumn Equinox, which Dawn could support by mandate. Alternatively, Varushka or Highguard could arm the orcish Dreamers of the Dark Forest if the Senate approved, or the Empire could permanently cede Echofell to the Thule. The Drownbark Forest could be protected by Dripping Echoes of the Fen, made permanent with 100 rings of ilium. Another option was a sovereign's offer to drown the forest, destroying the Palace of Orieb. The Cabalist of the Hollow Stone was charged with stopping the Druj at Marshstand Skerry.

n.Dawn: Lise de Lionsgate offered reworked plans for the Tower of the Manticore. A proposed Dawnish mandate would send knights-errant, questing knights and war witches to guard its construction and open a Secure the Echofell venture for Dawnish units.
n.Druj: Druj insurgents lurking in Echofell, the Drownbark Forest and the Webwood were the target of every option presented. Meanwhile warriors from across the Arkad, accompanied by heralds of the Burnt Steward, moved to destroy Marshstand Skerry.
n.Highguard: Naomi, herself Highborn, proposed that the Highborn assembly urge citizens to arm the Dreamers of the Dark Forest, echoing Highguard's old gifts of arms to the Imperial Orcs. Doing so would let Highborn units train the Dreamers, but only once the Senate authorised it.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Highborn soldiers once gave weapons and armour to the Imperial Orcs when they joined the Empire, and this was cited as a precedent for arming the Dreamers.
n.Thule: The Thule refused direct aid, saying the Empire had cooled on collaboration. They offered to deal with the Druj in both Echofell and their own Webwood if the Senate permanently ceded Echofell to them.
n.Varushka: Ossium's Senator Vesna Borkovna requested the appraisal, and Varushkan cabalists advised on Dripping Echoes of the Fen and on the Landgrave's offer. The Varushkan assembly could arm the Dreamers or approve the drowning of the Drownbark Forest, and Varushkan units could Seek Glory in the Twisted Woods once the Tower stood.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Webwood had been conceded to the Thule under the Winter treaty that secured their military aid in Sermersuaq.

t.Forest of Ulnak: Naomi identified the Druj-held Forest of Ulnak as the root of the threat. Any Ossium region that ceased to border Druj land there would be permanently secured, though an invasion would be blind and would face an immense fortification.
t.Ossium: Echofell, the Drownbark Forest and the Webwood remained under threat from the Druj, and the options to secure them ranged from fortifications and magic to ceding land to the Thule or flooding the eastern marshes. Marshstand Skerry also faced a direct Druj attack.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the Thule's military aid in Sermersuaq was secured by conceding the Webwood to them under the Winter treaty.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Dreamers of the Dark Forest were among the orc septs who chose not to relocate to Skarsind.

r.Ossium/Bittershore: Mentioned in passing: the Gryphon's Pride was setting up camps and resupplying in Bittershore when the Druj force was spotted.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: The marshy region could be protected by Dripping Echoes of the Fen, or drowned by the servants of the Landgrave of the Still Deeps' sovereign, which would sink the Palace of Orieb. A Druj force was heading through the Broken Clearing to destroy Marshstand Skerry.
r.Ossium/Echofell: Echofell could be secured by building a new Tower of the Manticore before the end of the Autumn Equinox, by arming the Dreamers of the Dark Forest with Senate approval, or by permanently ceding the region to the Thule, which would anger Cathan Canae.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: If the Landgrave's sovereign were allowed to flood the Drownbark Forest, Nearweald would also be affected and gain the marsh quality, making commissions there harder.
r.Ossium/Webwood: The Thule-held Webwood remained under Druj threat, with speculation about the Spider King's temple in its depths. The Thule promised to clear it of Druj if Echofell were ceded to them.

Deep forests and dark hills.d: A herald of Estavus offered the secret of a Forge of Hours at the Eternal Shafts of Time, letting the holder buy extra mithril with enchanted tools, available only while Estavus is not under enmity. A storytellers' Inn of the Granite Stag was proposed to let the Granites of Veltsgorsk yield more white granite. Varushkans proposed a Boyar of the Iron Roads, whose five offices would allow one extra ministry commission each season. The boyar of Triosk proposed the Eagle and Stag Exchange and the title of Eagle of Triosk, available until the end of Autumn Equinox 385YE. Northern trade ministries gained extra purchasing, and the Thule began selling mana for money to buy food.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Bonesetter of Torfast Trading Post in Skarsind gained an additional purchase rank on the eastern trade route, letting orc merchants buy more from Varushka.
n.Navarr: The Treji Wayhouse in Hercynia gained an additional ministry, giving Navarr's northern traders the chance to invest in Varushkan goods.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the boyar of Triosk modelled his proposed Eagle of Triosk title on what he had heard of the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills in Kahraman.
n.The League: Temeschwar's Northbound Trade gained an additional ministry for Varushkan goods, and the city's new mana exchange drew more Thule selling mana to the Keeper of the Tome at the expense of other trading partners.
n.Thule: Thule visiting Imperial markets, after negotiations with the Ambassador to Otkodov, began trading their crystal mana for money to buy large amounts of food to send north, with more selling to Temeschwar's new mana exchange.
n.Varushka: Varushka's people enjoyed a surge of trade, Pride and Prosperity, with opportunities to enhance its two Bourse seats, create a Boyar of the Iron Roads and build the Eagle and Stag Exchange in Triosk.
n.Wintermark: The Kalpaheim Tradeholder in Hahnmark gained an additional ministry allowing Wintermark's traders to invest in Varushkan goods.

t.Hahnmark: The Kalpaheim Tradeholder ministry here gained an additional ministry to purchase goods from Varushkan merchants.
t.Hercynia: The Treji Wayhouse here gained an additional ministry to purchase goods from Varushkan merchants.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills in Kahraman inspired the proposed Eagle of Triosk title.
t.Karov: A Forge of Hours could be built at the Eternal Shafts of Time to yield extra mithril, and the Custodian of the Assayer's Guild gained an extra ministry track as more traders brought fine metals through Karov.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Karsk's reclamation from the Thule left Triosk's old frontier barracks derelict and free to be repurposed.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: travellers from Miekarova pass through Triosk, which stands at a crossroads of the eastern vales.
t.Otkodov: The orcs of Otkodov shifted their trade, selling more mana in Temeschwar and seeking money rather than metals to buy food to send north.
t.Skarsind: The Torfast Trading Post here gained an additional purchase rank on the eastern trade route thanks to Varushka's prosperity.
t.Temeschwar: Northbound Trade gained an additional ministry, and the new Temeschwar Mana Exchange drew more Thule mana sellers to the Keeper of the Tome.
t.Volodmartz: Volodmartz was offered an Inn of the Granite Stag at Veltsgorsk to raise white granite output and the Eagle and Stag Exchange at Triosk to make the town a hub of Varushka's mineral trade.

r.Temeschwar/Metri: Mentioned in passing: the woods of Metri being safe to travel again helped more traders bring fine metals to the Assayer's Guild.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: An Inn of the Granite Stag for storytellers could be built at Veltsgorsk in the mountains of Brez, appeasing the quarry's dark influence and letting the Granites' holder buy more white granite.
r.Volodmartz/Livardz: Triosk's boyar proposed turning the town's derelict barracks into the Eagle and Stag Exchange, creating the Eagle of Triosk title able to buy metals and upgrade a mine each year.
r.Volodmartz/Opascari: Mentioned in passing: miners and wagon raiders bring metals and minerals from the mountains of Opascari to market in Triosk.

Farewell wanderlust.d: The enchantment touched only territories that were Imperial at the end of the Spring Equinox, including the newly conquered Barrens, but not Liathaven, Brocéliande, Feroz or Spiral. Lucky windfalls left every citizen at Anvil wealthier. Cambion felt Autumn's pull strongly. Businesses could diversify once without cost and gained new production options. The Bailiffs of the Guttered Flame offered vouchers for mithril, white granite and weirwood wains, though these were seized from the vaults of Pharam Vex and were surely proceeds of the slave trade. Deepstones appeared in the deepest mines. Farms yielded Ashen Residue instead of some produce, and forests yielded metallic fruit. Some Marcher farms with menhirs began turning into mana sites.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: a dusty bottle of century-old wine from the vineyards of Astolat is given as an example of a lucky find.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens, conquered from the Druj by Imperial heroes at the Battle of Merigionne, fell within the enchantment's reach.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Feroz, held by the Grendel, was outside the Empire's grasp and untouched by the enchantment.
n.Jotun: Liathaven, held by the Jotun, was untouched by the enchantment. The dissonant effects on farms and forests were nonetheless felt in Bregasland.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Siroc and Cargo are named among the places where the Bailiffs' otherworldly caravans emerged from Autumn regio.
n.The League: Bailiffs' caravans emerged around Tassato, Sarvos, Holberg and Temeschwar to bank materials for Bourse notes. Spiral lay outside the enchantment's reach, and a League theatre profited from a crowd-pleasing new play about Basileus Flint and Spiral.
n.The Marches: Marcher farms with more than two sets of menhirs began transforming into mana sites. The Circle of the Rosy Rook of Wayford offered to dismantle the menhirs for farmers who wished to keep their farms, paying a throne per set.
n.Urizen: An Urizen magician who oversees ushabti labourers studied the ruined farm produce and published findings showing that it was rich in useful Autumn magic.
n.Wintermark: The Net and Vine of Wintermark performed the Bounty of the Brilliant Broker, the first Imperial enchantment tied to the realm of Autumn, which caused all these effects.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: wine from the vineyards of Astolat is cited as an example of a serendipitous find.
t.Bregasland: Although untouched by the Spring Hallow, Bregasland still felt the dissonant effects on farm and forest produce.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Brocéliande was not Imperial at the end of the Spring Equinox, so the enchantment did not affect it.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Feroz was excluded from the enchantment, so businesses there could not gain its benefits.
t.Hahnmark: Otherworldly caravans of the Bailiffs of the Guttered Flame emerged from Autumn regio around Kalpaheim to bank magical materials.
t.Holberg: Bailiffs' caravans drawn by six-legged lead-scaled lizards emerged from Autumn regio around Holberg, unloading materials in exchange for Bourse notes.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven was outside the enchantment's reach.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Siroc and Cargo are listed among the places where the Bailiffs' caravans appeared.
t.Mitwold: Bailiffs' caravans emerged around Meade, while Marcher farms with menhirs began turning into mana sites.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is used as an example of an affected territory where a cambion might have spent the season.
t.Sarvos: Bailiffs' caravans emerged from Autumn regio around Sarvos. A lost Throne coin feeding a Sarvosan orphan is cited as a lucky windfall.
t.Spiral: Spiral lay outside the enchantment's reach, though a new League play about Spiral and the Keeper of the Black Vaults was drawing full houses.
t.Tassato: Bailiffs of the Guttered Flame caravans emerged from Autumn regio around Tassato to bank mithril, white granite and weirwood.
t.Temeschwar: Bailiffs' caravans emerged from Autumn regio around Temeschwar, depositing materials in Imperial warehouses for Bourse notes.
t.The Barrens: Newly conquered at the Battle of Merigionne, the Barrens fell within the enchantment's reach, and its farms and forests felt the dissonant effects.

Fate and function.d: The Crucible, built under the Master of the Koboldi and hastened by Autumn magic, was endorsed by a greater-majority Urizen Assembly mandate carried by Able of Zenith Ascendant. Zenith lost its bereft of hope and stifled by miasma qualities. Settlers returned to build compact, defensible spires, helped by new ushabti and Adamant's koboldi, who were allowed to live beneath the Crucible. Prospero's incentives saw the heliopticon towers repaired. Ushabti cut the cost of boosting Urizeni mines, forests and herb gardens. An Architect of the Crucible title was to go to the Senate, with powers to commission ushabti, buy staves and buy ilium found by Estavus's bronze birds. Rival Synod mandates proposed a Prosperity shrine or a tomb to Achilles.

n.Druj: The miasma and despair the Druj left behind in Zenith were finally dispelled, though scattered remnants of their malice still lurk in the territory's dark corners and their marks will take a generation to heal.
n.Navarr: A proposed tomb to the exemplar Achilles at the Crucible risks unexpected consequences for Navarr, since he was murdered by a Navarr citizen, apparently of the Quiet Step, barely three years earlier, a killing still unsolved despite Idanach Listing Beacon's condemnation.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Achilles's home of Damakhan's Forge is noted as soon to be in a League territory, one reason given for memorialising him at the Crucible instead.
n.Urizen: Urizen gained a new arete founded on commerce and craftsmanship. Citizens could move resources to Zenith on favourable terms, pay less to increase mine, forest and herb garden production, and potentially gain an Architect of the Crucible with valuable powers.

t.Morrow: Many refugees from Zenith had settled in Morrow, and the repaired heliopticon restored swift communication with it. Resources there may be upgraded through the Architect's bespoke ushabti, and the faithful were urged to gather there for a consecration before travelling to Iteri.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt had taken in Zenith's refugees, some of whom are content to stay. The heliopticon now links it again with Zenith, and its resources are eligible for upgrades through the Crucible's bespoke ushabti.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos's reinvention as the City of Masks is cited as a comparable, though less ambitious, example of a new story reshaping a territory.
t.Zenith: Zenith shed its bereft of hope and stifled by miasma qualities. Settlers began raising new, defensible spires, the heliopticon towers were repaired, and Urizen characters gained a temporary chance to relocate resources there until the Autumn Equinox.

r.Zenith/Iteri: The Crucible of Fate stands in Iteri, producing ushabti and magic items, housing Adamant's koboldi in tunnels beneath it, and offered as the site of a possible Prosperity shrine or a tomb to Achilles.
r.Zenith/Lustri: Mentioned in passing: work on the defences being built in Lustri helps ease fears that the Druj will soon return.

Four and four.d: Barien's heralds were to hold court with House Geris in Wintermark and asked Wintermark's artisans to choose a schema. Janon's heralds fought beside the Burning Falcon in Kahraman, offered to join any general's army, and proposed ways to give the army True Conviction; more would visit the Imperial Orcs. Kimus challenged the Synod to explain what happens after death. Lashonar asked Eliza of Sarvos to rescue its herald Decius from Druj in Nesustak Forest. With its enmity lifted, Siakha's heralds stirred trouble across the Empire, marched from Semmerholm and challenged Mitwold travellers to fights. Tharim sought cursed Sarcophan curios, Ylenwe offered restitution, and Zakalwe rewarded Dawn's strategists and approached Wintermark and the Orcs.

n.Dawn: Zakalwe's herald Agon was to reward the Dawnish team from the Great Game, Janon's heralds sought Kahendrin Wordsmith, and Siakha's heralds goaded people into settling old scores in Dawn.
n.Druj: A Druj force of Arkad warriors and heralds of the Ashen Knight was hunting Lashonar's herald Decius in the Sarangrave, and a Druj ghulai held and befouled the Swan's Chalice.
n.Highguard: Ylenwe offered to help with the beacon of the Way in the White City if the enmity were removed and the General Assembly or Highborn National Assembly invited zie by statement of principle.
n.Imperial Orcs: Janon's heralds planned to visit the Orc camp to speak with the shatterers of chains, especially Ashborn Pakt, and Zakalwe's herald Asp was to discuss devising a new strategy game for the nation.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun were the foe the Burning Falcon fought in Kahraman with Janon's heralds alongside.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Spider King's support for some Navarr armies was cited as a model for Janon's proposed watch over the Burning Falcon.
n.The Brass Coast: Janon's heralds fought with the Burning Falcon, and the eternal offered ways, via a Freeborn assembly statement or a ritual using his token and 25 rings of ilium, for the army to gain True Conviction.
n.The League: Eliza of Sarvos was asked by Lashonar to save its herald from the Druj, and Siakha's heralds encouraged violence and theft in the League.
n.The Marches: Siakha's heralds were challenging Mitwold travellers to fights to the death, and Sally Thresher of House Talbot was asked to deal with them; similar incidents occurred elsewhere in the Marches.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka was one of the nations where Siakha's heralds egged people on to settle old scores.
n.Wintermark: House Geris was to host Barien's heralds, Wintermark's artisans had to choose the schema Barien owed them, and Zakalwe sought Wintermark strategists for the next stage of the Great Game.

t.Bastion: Ylenwe expressed interest in contributing belltowers to the planned beacon of the Way in the White City, subject to the enmity being lifted and an invitation from the Synod.
t.Kahraman: Janon's midnight-blue heralds fought alongside the Burning Falcon in the battles to retake Kahraman from the Jotun, with little effect on the outcome.
t.Mitwold: More than half a dozen Siakha heralds were challenging travellers on the little-used track from Odd's End to Hay to fights to the death, and someone was suspected of having made a deal with them.
t.Sarangrave: Lashonar's herald Decius was trapped and pursued by Druj and Surut's heralds, the Druj miasma threatened any rescuers, and a ghulai there held the Swan's Chalice.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Eliza, the magician Lashonar asked to rescue its herald, hails from Sarvos.
t.Semmerholm: A posse of armed shark-like Siakha heralds and glowing changeling-like creatures emerged from Semmerholm and set off on foot for Anvil, following their prey.

r.Kahraman/Gambit: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, though the page refers to battles to retake Kahraman generally.
r.Mitwold/Golden Downs: The Sentinel Gate was to open to the Long Road in Golden Downs so threshers could confront the Siakha heralds challenging locals to fights.
r.Mitwold/Oddmire: Mentioned in passing: the troubled track begins at Odd's End before running towards Hay.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: Decius Frostspire took refuge in the Thicket of Thorns in Nesustak Forest, where the Sentinel Gate was to open for a rescue against the pursuing Druj.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: For several seasons bodies had been found gouged in Axmure's waters and dire beasts rumoured in its woods, before Siakha's heralds left for Anvil.

Half-time score.d: Fransesca di Matos's competition counted commissions and personal resource upgrades alike. After two seasons the scores stood at Temeschwar 120, Holberg 90, Sarvos 47 and Tassato 33. Temeschwar was offered two great works, new mining roads or the Vardstein Timber mill, and both would raise Imperial taxes. Holberg could help the Sand Fishers start their sawmills through a 50-throne loan endorsed by a League Assembly mandate. Sarvos faced a possible Grendel threat as the peace treaty neared its end, and its merchant princes offered to match white granite given to the Chain Against Chains coastal fortification. Genia Bourné extended her brokers office offer. Tassato was offered a great statue of Barell, a founder of the League.

n.Grendel: With their peace treaty due to expire and three armadas off the Imperial coast, the Grendel were seen as a serious threat to Sarvos, which they had sacked once before. They were expected to be angered by Spiral joining the League.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the League's founders sought a nation of equal power and importance to Highguard and the other nations.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun destroyed the Sapphire Stair in Tassato, and rebuilding it would need 30 wains.
n.The League: The League's cities were competing to out-build one another. Its National Assembly was asked to mandate a citizen to lend the Sand Fishers 50 thrones, and its people were offered opportunities ranging from fortifications to a statue of the founder Barell.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: historical accounts describe Barell as proud leader of the greatest city on the Bay of Catazar.
t.Holberg: Holberg ran second with 90 wains, helped by Kleist's Winter Gardens and by citizens upgrading their personal resources. A loan to the Sand Fishers could let them start their sawmills and add 30 wains to the city's total.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos trailed with 47 wains and stayed in the race only through individual citizens. It faced a looming Grendel threat, and the Chain Against Chains fortification, the Glass Palace, the Greatest Taste and Genia Bourné's brokers office were all offered as opportunities.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Spiral had just joined the League, which was expected to anger the Grendel.
t.Tassato: Tassato looked set to finish last with 33 wains, mostly from repairs to the Blood Red River museum, and had suffered the loss of the Sapphire Stair to the Jotun. A 75-wain statue of Barell was proposed to restore the city's Pride.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar led with 120 wains, largely thanks to the new Department of Architecture, but personal investment there had been low. Two great works were proposed, mining roads and a timber mill, which would add 5 and 10 thrones a season to Imperial taxes respectively.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: completed Sand Fisher sawmills would leave them well placed to help the League build a port on the Semmerlak.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: Misericorde was one site of the Sand Fishers' planned sawmills, the Just Rewards sinecure, and its market's merchant princes had kept the orcs supplied with the resources they had saved.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: Utterlund was the other site of the Sand Fishers' planned sawmills, which a League loan could allow them to begin at once.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: Cigno was the location of the Chain Against Chains, a coastal fortification needing 130 wains of white granite, which Sarvos merchants offered to support with matching contributions for two seasons.
r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: The proposed statue of Barell would stand in the Vassa with arms outstretched between Mestra and Regario as a symbol of their unity.
r.Tassato/Tassato Regario: Regario would be joined symbolically to Mestra by the proposed statue of Barell standing in the river between them.
r.Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale: Marina Pretensa proposed the Vardstein Timber mill and Sorting Yard on the edge of the Vale, with a road to the city, to supply forest materials to Temeschwar's businesses and create a new Imperial title.

Improve the vale of Orieb.d: Proposed by Karsk and seconded by Miekarova, the motion expanded Orieb as set out in the Thousands or more wind of fortune, using a single commission slot. It cost 10 wains of mithril, 10 wains of white granite and 6 thrones in labour (raised from 5 because the site lies in a marsh), and takes three months to build. After the Summer Solstice the materials and money were supplied, chiefly by Krasivit Buhkova, with further crowns and granite from Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov, Velko Perunovich Razoradze, Fintan Nighthaven, Sławomir Rabovich Bolotstrazh and Triska Markova. Once complete, the Merchant-Boyar of the Stinking Market gains 5 crowns a season and two new ministry tracks offering magic weapons and armour, and herbs from Ossium's eastern forests.

n.Varushka: Varushkan senators proposed the motion and Varushkan citizens largely paid for it, gaining a first true vale in the Drownbark and a richer Merchant-Boyar of the Stinking Market.

t.Ossium: Ossium gains an expanded Orieb, whose Stinking Market will offer magic arms and armour and herbs from the territory's eastern forests once construction is complete.

r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: The Drownbark Forest is to receive its first true vale at Orieb, a three-month build in marshland that drove the labour cost up to 6 thrones.

Inkpot gods.d: Ephisis changed how Ephisis' Scale worked for the solstice and offered a Golden Market of Aggido, a vis market to be built in Anozel, Ashill or Gildenheim by wayleave. Callidus sought liao and true liao, and offered Jarmish white seed to one nation chosen by the Synod. His associate Sanvar Isk offered access to Prospero's Loom of Spells. Estavus held a fire sale of magical items, offered schema to Wintermark and proposed a fane in Proceris. Prospero offered diplomatic favours, including keeping Jarm out of the Grendel war. Flint offered a surprise attack opportunity if Axos was cut from the Liberty Pact. Mazen's boons ceased working, and Autumn boggarts spread mischief.

n.Grendel: Prospero offered to use his influence so that Jarm would stop aiding the Grendel in their coming war with the Empire. Flint revealed he had urged a surprise attack on the Grendel in Feroz, which the Military Council had declined.
n.Imperial Orcs: Golden Consortium agents had been active in Skarsind, and Needa's Hall near Gildenheim was offered as one possible site for the Golden Market of Aggido.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Estavus is described as a firm ally of the Jotun, supplying them with weapons and warriors against the Empire.
n.The Brass Coast: Golden Consortium agents had been active in Segura, and an abandoned parador in the struggling town of Anozel was offered as a possible site for the Golden Market of Aggido.
n.The League: Sanvar Isk found an anchor in Tassato Mestra for linking the Loom of Spells to the Empire. Meanwhile silver-skinned Autumn creatures harassed homesteaders in Madeiras.
n.The Marches: Golden Consortium agents had been active in Upwold, and Quick Alice offered the Grosvenor family home in Ashill as a possible site for the Golden Market of Aggido.
n.Urizen: Scores of Estavus's heralds emerged around Zenith. The Forgemistress proposed a Fane of Shadows in Proceris, with Urizen to appoint an Architect who could buy her heralds' magical items.
n.Wintermark: Estavus offered Wintermark's artisans five schema for sale during the solstice, on the strict condition that any purchased were added to Runesmith's Law at Runegrott.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Flint's heralds had proposed a surprise attack on the Grendel in Feroz last season, which the Military Council declined.
t.Hahnmark: Estavus offered schema on condition that any purchased were added to the body of lore kept at Runegrott under Runesmith's Law.
t.Segura: Golden Consortium agents had been active in Segura and identified an abandoned parador in Anozel as a candidate site for their vis market.
t.Skarsind: Golden Consortium agents had been active in Skarsind. Needa's Hall, a ruined meadery near Gildenheim, was offered as a candidate site for the Golden Market.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Flint's heralds cited Kaliact's betrayal of the Grendel in Spiral as an example of profitable treachery.
t.Tassato: An Autumn regio in Tassato Mestra could anchor the Loom of Spells, while realm-creatures in Madeiras demanded pay for unasked-for work.
t.Upwold: Golden Consortium agents had been active in Upwold. The Grosvenor home in the charcoal-burning village of Ashill was offered as a candidate market site.
t.Zenith: Estavus's heralds emerged in large numbers around Zenith in response to the Autumn Archmage's plea for help rebuilding, and a fane was proposed in Proceris.

r.Tassato/Madeiras: Mobs of silver-skinned realm-creatures in the forests demanded pay for unrequested work and carted off homesteaders' crates, nails and tools.
r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: Sanvar Isk located a site here to anchor the Loom of Spells. Connecting it required one hundred ingots or measures during the Summer Solstice.
r.Upwold/Ashbrook: Ashbrook was a permitted location for the Golden Market of Aggido, via the Grosvenor family home in Ashill, which was in need of repairs that would accommodate mithril tie beams.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Estavus was intrigued by the nightwoven marshes and proposed a Fane of Shadows here, costing 10 wains of mithril, 10 rings of ilium and 20 crowns, if her heralds were allowed to study them.

Murder of Crows.d: Cynerik's judgement called for Yulia to be interred in Kallavesa's Sovevann marshes. She had backed the Thule alliance that freed Sermersuaq, and Varushka revoked her for it. No one not of the Mark had ever been interred there, and the marsh-keepers urged caution. The alternatives were to write her in the Chronicle of Heroism, adopt her into Wintermark, or seek recognition of her as an exemplar. Dogri, already chronicled, could be made an exemplar, given a tomb, or honoured with a Crows Ridge memorial that would spark an uprising against the Thule. Ingrid Seiging's judgement raised the option of a mandate to drop "fight with honour" and wage ruthless war on the Jotun.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Dogri Thulebane is said to have died fighting the Grendel in service to the Empire.
n.Imperial Orcs: Dogri's legend grew from his refusal to leave Crows Ridge when the Empire gave Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs in 379YE. Making him an exemplar would ensure that no Wintermark land could again be given away without a fight.
n.Jotun: Wintermark could abandon its honourable way of fighting the Jotun and refuse to let them recover their wounded, killing as many as possible. Doing so would throw away any rapport that restraint had built.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr are cited as having seized every opportunity to slaughter the Jotun, which may have hindered any rapprochement.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Jarl of Kierheim has said the war cannot end while Jotun who bear the shame of their failure in Mournwold still live.
n.Thule: The Thule alliance that freed Sermersuaq lies at the heart of Yulia's story. A Wintermark memorial to Dogri in Crows Ridge would provoke uprisings against Thule-held land, shattering relations and risking war or demands for reparations.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Yulia was mortally wounded on the battlefields of Zenith before dying on the Throne in Anvil.
n.Varushka: Yulia, a Varushkan senator, was revoked and shunned by her own Assembly for supporting Wintermark. Mystics warned that honouring her in the Chronicle of Heroism would bring good fortune unlikely to please the Varushkans.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark Assembly faced compatible choices on honouring Yulia and Dogri, including an unprecedented interment in the Sovevann and a provocative memorial at Crows Ridge. It also had to decide whether to end its honourable conduct of war against the Jotun.

t.Kallavesa: The Sovevann marshes could receive Yulia's body, a step never before taken for anyone not of the Mark, with uncertain effects on the spirits there. A virtue assembly could also raise an inspirational tomb to Dogri there, drawing pilgrims from across the Empire.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Yulia had been senator for Miekarova, and the judgement says she sacrificed her homeland to help Wintermark reclaim Sermersuaq.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun failure in Mournwold is cited as a reason the Jarl of Kierheim says the war cannot end.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Otkodov, Yevgeni Katzev, spoke in support of the Thule alliance and later faced Varushkan censure.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq was freed from Jotun rule by the Thule alliance Yulia championed. A Dogri memorial would send Wintermark insurgents against the Thule-held Silver Peaks.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: it is not named directly, and is touched only through the wider Wintermark–Jotun war the page discusses.
t.Skarsind: Dogri defied the Senate's gift of Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs by holding Crows Ridge, now in Thule hands. A Wintermark memorial there would spark an uprising against its fortifications that would fail without Imperial armies or many military units.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Yulia was mortally wounded on the battlefields of Zenith.

r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: If Wintermark consecrated a memorial to Dogri in Crows Ridge, inspired young Wintermarkers would attack the fortified Silver Peaks. The attack would fail without strong support and would sour relations with the Thule.

Not a drop to drink.d: The blight is driven by Dry Patricians, intelligent creatures akin to ushabti, and by the Parched who are slowly becoming them. Regrow the Land's Heart has kept the blight from spreading but cannot weaken it. If the ritual is cast every season, the Great Grasses would be lost to desert by Winter 385YE but the blight held at its borders. Making it permanent would need 120 rings of ilium. Missing a single season risked desertification across Madruga, including Siroc. Three conjunctions were offered: the Champion of Loyalty, Dagon, could recover a living Tutamen survivor; Grandmaster Eliza could escort Unfettered Mind scholars to a minor Winter regio; and Senator Chiara Zayden Riqueza could stop Dry Patricians gathering at a powerful regio.

n.Highguard: Unconquered from Syrene suspect the blight's Aldea di Tutamen family descends from the Tutamen, a pre-revelation Highborn patrician family. They asked the Champion of Loyalty to recover a living survivor dressed as a Highborn magister.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun-held Bregasland is home to the Landskeeper tradition of the Marcher scholar Barti Dourfen.
n.Navarr: The Navarri vate Merry Songbird's Passing wished to study the blight as a possible Winter-fuelled vallorn and sought fellow Navarr to escort her. She hoped Navarr understanding of the Dance of Navarr and Thorn might be turned against it.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn faced losing the Great Grasses, and potentially all of Madruga including Siroc, unless Regrow the Land's Heart was cast every season. Some Freeborn muttered that this was the Empire's own vallorn, and the Senator for Madruga was charged with confronting the Dry Patricians.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: an ancestor of the orc shaman Frostbiter Grik had been enslaved by a Thule warlock who experimented with Winter magic to blight the land.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Dry Patricians were likened to the ushabti of Urizen, creatures closer to enchanted objects than truly living beings.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the scholar Barti Dourfen comes from a proud tradition of Bregas Landskeepers and proposed using standing stones to contain or redirect the blight.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: a group of unconquered from Syrene had been asking about the Aldea di Tutamen family and its possible Highborn ancestry.
t.Madruga: The Great Grasses faced being lost to a deadly desert, held at its borders only if Regrow the Land's Heart was cast every season. A missed season risked spreading desertification to Siroc, Cazar, Qatar and Trajadoz, and possibly beyond Madruga.

Pride and prejudice.d: Velko Perunovich Razoradze and Jared of the Suns of Couros spread the mandates. Short of food, the Thule offered more ilium if a High Path were cut from Brez into Otkodov. The warlock Orathator offered magical masks in return for access to the Well of Shadows or the ritual Delve Deep, Beneath the Mountain. The Mirnatocz warlocks offered red moss for a warehouse at Ivarsgard, and rival mandates proposed stealing or protecting its secret. The Leshun of Branoc agreed to a market and a Speaker. The Menrothat sought Farweald and offered help with shrines at Orieb. Highguard proposed aid to Thule former slaves. Anti-orc prejudice continued to erode.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is not named, but it shares the Barrens, where the Menrothat want their ancestral heartland of Farweald returned.
n.Druj: The Druj once ruled Ossium and used the Palace of Orieb. Menrothat still under their yoke in the Forest of Ulnak, or serving as their scouts, risk reprisals if the sept cooperates too closely with the Empire.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly backed the Varushkan outreach and proved useful in talks with the Leshun. They were offered mandates to have the unconquered steal the red moss secret and to send secret aid to Thule former slaves, though a Varushkan counter-mandate threatened to turn Highborn soldiers back by force.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orcs helped make first contact with the Menrothat, and they have agreed to receive the sept's single dose of black lotus and knowledge of its use if Farweald is given to the Menrothat.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: negotiations took place at a Navarr wayhouse in Srodkoja, and Navarr helped make first contact with the Menrothat, likening them to the feni.
n.Thule: The Thule, struggling to feed their freed slaves, offered more ilium for Varushkan food via the High Path, and their warlocks offered masks and red moss in trade. They faced possible theft of the red moss secret and covert Highborn aid to their underclass, both of which would anger the Dragons.
n.Varushka: Varushka led the outreach to orcs and gained opportunities to trade with the Thule, the Leshun and the Menrothat, along with competing mandates over the red moss. The episode further eroded traditional Varushkan prejudice against orcs.

t.Forest of Ulnak: Menrothat still under Druj rule here risk reprisals if their sept cooperates with the Empire, and the Dreamers of the Dark Forest have been asked for help against the threat of Druj invasion from here.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Delev Market in Karov is noted as the main existing route for quiet trade with the Thule.
t.Karsk: Karsk held several of the opportunities: masks for the Warden of the Trees and Hills at Ivarsgard, red moss from the Thule warlocks of Mirnatocz in exchange for a warehouse at the Sarcophan Mooring, and the Leshun Market in Branoc. A Varushkan counter-mandate could bring fighting with the Highborn here.
t.Miekarova: Orathator is based in Thule-held Miechernya and regularly visits the Butterfly Holt, where he offered masks to the Gloaming Sentinel. He seeks the Well of Shadows, which he believes lies somewhere in the territory.
t.Ossium: The Menrothat live in Ossium as guests of the Varushkans, offering guides, workers and help restoring vis-giving shrines at the Palace of Orieb. A Varushkan counter-mandate could bring fighting with the Highborn here.
t.Otkodov: The Thule homeland faces food shortages after the slaves were freed. The High Path through the mountains was opened so that Varushkan food could be traded for ilium from the fallen star in Sküld.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Well of Shadows once stood in Skarsind as Pakaanan's Tower, and the Highborn could reach Miechernya through the territory.
t.The Barrens: The Menrothat regard Farweald in the northern Barrens as their ancestral heartland and want it restored to them. The Highborn drew on recent experience in the Barrens when dealing with the Leshun.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: Ivarsgard, one of Orathator's regular stops, lies on the edge of the Semmerlak.
t.Volodmartz: The High Path to Otkodov was built from Brez. The Leshun also have ties with orc settlements in Volodmartz.

r.Karsk/Branoc: The Sept of the Leshun near Broken Hill agreed to formal trade, and a market creating the title of Speaker to the Leshun was commissioned here.
r.Karsk/Crowslook: Mentioned in passing: Mirnatocz in Krevsaty stood near the border with Crowslook.
r.Karsk/Krevsaty: In this Thule-held region, the warlocks of the Mirnatocz tower offered red moss in trade, and rival mandates proposed either stealing its secret or preventing any such raid.
r.Karsk/Nitrost: Mentioned in passing: orc settlements here were conquered by the Thule in 368YE, and their people fled to Branoc.
r.Miekarova/Miechernya: This Thule-held region is Orathator's base and a target for closer trade. The Highborn could reach it through Skarsind even if Varushka blocked their route.
r.Miekarova/Srodkoja: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan and Highborn pilgrims negotiated with Orathator at a Navarr wayhouse here.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: Mentioned in passing: the Bonewood is Thule-controlled, and the Thule freed Druj slaves from it during the liberation of Ossium.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Mentioned in passing: some Menrothat live in the eastern Drownbark Forest.
r.Ossium/Echofell: Mentioned in passing: some Menrothat live in south-eastern Echofell.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: The Menrothat sept is based in Nearweald and provides guides, workers and tithes to nearby vales.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Mentioned in passing: the Webwood is listed among the regions controlled by the Thule.
r.Otkodov/Nithoggir: Mentioned in passing: Orathator suspects the catacomb-library of Nithoggir holds a ritual like Delve Deep, Beneath the Mountain, but he cannot access it.
r.The Barrens/Farweald: The Menrothat seek the return of Farweald, their ancestral heartland, offering strong trade with Varushka and black lotus to the Imperial Orcs in exchange.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: The Gift of the Dwindling Star in Brez was the starting point of the High Path, completed before the Autumn Equinox 385YE so that its holder could buy up to four extra rings of Thule ilium.

Pruning shears.d: Benson was recognised as an exemplar of Vigilance in 379YE but remains little known outside the Marches. In Spring 385YE the Marcher Assembly passed Rowan Harper's judgement by greater majority, but Martin Orchard's General Assembly judgement fell short of one. A conjunction of unstable size, currently twenty, lets Martin Orchard lead Marchers to consecrate the orchard with true liao. Proposed mandates included: sending Upwold pilgrims to seek out dangers in the territory; competing Marcher mandates freeing threshers against the Whisper Gallery, either in the Marches or in Tassato, each costing mana production; and a Highborn mandate urging inquisitors and magisters to hunt Gallery cultists in Highguard.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Benson is believed to have taken part in the March from Dawn, and his recognition credits him with saving Dawnish as well as Marcher souls.
n.Highguard: Aemon of the Suns of Couros proposed a Highborn mandate urging inquisitors and magisters to hunt Whisper Gallery cultists in Highguard. It would cost every Highborn mana site one crystal until Winter 385YE in exchange for a chance to ensnare a major Gallery agent.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the war in Bregasland is cited as the matter keeping Upwold's folk too busy to pry into their neighbours' business.
n.The League: Martin Orchard proposed a Marcher mandate sending threshers into Tassato after Whisper Gallery allies. This would bring street fighting and lost mana to the League territory.
n.The Marches: Marchers could consecrate Benson's grave-orchard to Vigilance and might pass mandates for Upwold pilgrims to root out hidden dangers. They might also let threshers hunt the Whisper Gallery beyond the bounds of law, at a cost to every Marcher mana site and monolith farm.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the war in Bregasland is described as the focus of most folk's attention in neighbouring Upwold.
t.Tassato: A proposed Marcher mandate would send threshers into Tassato, the first home of Berechiah, to hunt the Whisper Gallery. It would cause armed clashes in the streets and cost every mana site two crystals after the Summer Solstice.
t.Upwold: Pickham Monastery's grave-orchard in Upwold could be consecrated to Vigilance. A proposed mandate would send Upwold's Vigilant pilgrims hunting heretics, traitors and other threats, with a report of active dangers due at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

r.Upwold/Tower March: The Sentinel Gate opened to Benson's Orchard in Tower March, letting around twenty Marchers led by Martin Orchard consecrate the exemplar's resting place to Vigilance with true liao.

Questions of virtue.d: The Jotun withdrew from Kahraman into Liaven's Glen, leaving champions who had survived Orchard's Watch to fight to the death under empty red banners at Fort Braydon. A Highborn priest urged the Freeborn to decide the fate of the bodies: competing mandates offered a Jotun burial mound, return of the corpses to the Jotun borders, a Freeborn pyre, or looting them and leaving them for carrion, which would make the Jotun treat the Freeborn like the Navarr. Highguard could mandate support for Freeborn armies in the Brass Coast and Feroz. Tharim offered 1,000 knights for a year in exchange for feasting on Freeborn mana sites and herb gardens. After Asavea destroyed the Isle of the Osseini and Shantarim, corsairs could be urged to vengeance, to break the Sumaah blockade, or to guard the Bay.

n.Dawn: Tharim's agreement to help Dawn retake the Barrens had just expired, and he proposed sending the knights stationed there to the Fire of the South instead.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun insult the Navarr as 'Imperial Druj', and the Freeborn were judged unlikely to honour Druj customs under one mandate.
n.Grendel: Grendel-held Feroz was named as a target the Highborn could help the Freeborn reclaim, and Tharim's knights would fight the Grendel as well as the Jotun; the destruction of Osseini and Shantarim was carried out by their Asavean allies.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly, acting on its peerless kinship, could mandate that Highborn armies and units fighting in the Brass Coast or Feroz gain bonuses until Summer 386YE, and could also send its fleets to help thwart the Asavean blockade of Sumaah.
n.Jotun: The Jotun left Kahraman, their champions from Orchard's Watch dying at Fort Braydon to expunge their shame, and how the Freeborn treat the bodies would shape Jotun views of the Brass Coast, possibly leading them to treat it like the Navarr.
n.Navarr: The Jotun reserve particular hatred for the Navarr, Navarr soldiers fought at Fort Braydon and argued against honouring the dead, and a contemptuous treatment of the bodies would see the Freeborn regarded much as the Navarr are.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn Assembly faced competing mandates on the Jotun dead, on corsair vengeance or the Sumaah blockade, and on a proposed naming convention for newcomers, while Highguard and Tharim offered aid amid the looming threat from the Broken Shore.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun champions had fought in the Mournwold and survived Orchard's Watch, shamed by their failure to protect the thralls of the Mournwold.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn's earlier help in reclaiming Zenith was cited as a model for aiding the Freeborn.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: adding a fourth Freeborn tribe was likened to Wintermark developing a new tradition.

t.Bay of Catazar: One proposed mandate would have Freeborn corsairs forgo vengeance and instead guard the Bay against barbarians.
t.Feroz: The Isle of the Osseini and Shantarim in Feroz were destroyed by Asavean warships, ending the Justicars, and a Highborn mandate could aid Freeborn armies seeking to retake the Grendel-held territory.
t.Kahraman: The Jotun abandoned Kahraman after raiding across the Cinnabar Hills, leaving its people to decide how to deal with the champions slain at Fort Braydon.
t.Liathaven: The Jotun withdrew into Liathaven, and one mandate would see cartloads of Jotun dead carried to its borders.
t.Madruga: With the peace treaty ending, an invasion of Madruga by the orcs of the Broken Shore was considered almost inevitable, and Highborn aid against the Dry Patricians there was suggested.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the fallen Jotun champions were veterans of the Mournwold fighting at Orchard's Watch.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: one mandate would return the Jotun bodies to the borders of Reinos and Liathaven.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Segura was noted as sharing a long border with Jotun lands, open to renewed invasion.
t.The Barrens: Tharim's knights in the Barrens, whose deal with Dawn had expired, would leave to join the Fire of the South if the Freeborn accepted his offer.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Highborn help in reclaiming Zenith was cited as precedent.

r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: The last Jotun encampment around Fort Braydon fought to the death here, and the Freeborn must decide whether their bodies are mounded, burned, returned or left for carrion.
r.Liathaven/Liaven's Glen: The Jotun retreated from Kahraman back into Liaven's Glen before the Imperial armies arrived.

Raise Dawnish army Summer 385YE.d: The motion to disburse funds for a Dawnish army was proposed by Astolat and seconded by Kallavesa. It passed at 250 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Astolat. The Speaker for the Senate also raised an administrative motion amending it, and that amendment passed. Construction required 200 wains of mithril and 50 thrones over a year. These were supplied in instalments from Autumn 385YE to Winter 386YE. The largest donors were Vesna Borkovna Prochnost and Bohemond De Rondell, with further crowns and rings from Aliss Thorn, Agoval of house Meliora, Farren Silver Streams and others. Once complete, the Lions of Adelmar took their place as the fourth Dawnish army.

n.Dawn: Dawn gained a fourth army, the Lions of Adelmar, adding to the nation's military strength once the required mithril and money had been gathered.

t.Astolat: The army was raised in Astolat, whose Senator proposed the motion and received the 250 thrones disbursed to fund it.

Reconstruct Gardens of Pallas.d: Nikolai, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the reconstruction, taking advantage of the previous season's appraisal and following a withdrawn Senate motion. It required 30 wains of weirwood, 12 wains of mithril, 116 crowns in labour and three months to build. Funding came slowly from many donors, including Anastasia, Bartimaeus, Fintan and Rhys Nighthaven, Richardo Glostari di Sarvos, Juno of Lapis Heights and Serenus Starsong. Esteban Ezmara of Sarangrave Reforged supplied the bulk of the mithril, weirwood and money after the Winter Solstice 385YE and Summer Solstice 386YE. With the Gardens complete, the senators of Urizen could appoint the Gardener of Pallas for the first time at the Autumn Equinox 386YE.

n.Urizen: Urizen's senators gain a new sinecure, the Gardener of Pallas, which they could appoint for the first time at the Autumn Equinox 386YE.

t.Zenith: Zenith gained a restored landmark when the Gardens of Pallas were rebuilt within its borders, creating a new sinecure tied to the territory.

r.Zenith/Proceris: The Gardens of Pallas were reconstructed in Proceris, a project completed after the Summer Solstice 386YE with 30 wains of weirwood and 12 wains of mithril.

Restoration and renewal.d: The Senate asked for an appraisal of the Gardens of Pallas, a Urizen herb-garden sinecure in Iteri smashed and burned by the Druj. Rebuilding would cost 20 wains of weirwood, 40 crowns and three months, creating a Gardener of Pallas title. Lutomysla proposed optional improvements. These were specialised ushabti from the Crucible of Fate costing 4 Thrones, and a Nightwoven site in Proceris to grow realmsroot. Others were the return of Bleak Tower herbalists through a Urizen National Assembly mandate, and support from Fountainhome Spire magicians, which depends on Ossegrahn not being declared an enemy. A Sadogua herald held by Lumi of Wintermark could also be moved with Lumi's permission. All the options lapsed if not commissioned that Solstice.

n.Druj: The Druj had thoroughly destroyed the gardens and their ushabti, and the proposal sought to turn the lingering Night magic they left in Proceris to Imperial advantage.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel aggression is named as one reason refugees, including the Fountainhome Spire magicians, fled Spiral.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the League appears only through Spiral, the territory from which the Fountainhome Spire refugees had fled.
n.Urizen: Urizen could regain its lost herb-garden sinecure, enhanced by ushabti from the Crucible of Fate. Its National Assembly was offered a mandate to persuade Bleak Tower herbalists to return to Zenith.
n.Wintermark: Lumi of Wintermark could allow the Silent Gardener, Sadogua's herald working at Lumi's Teahouse, to move to the new gardens and grow realmsroot there. Doing so would mean losing that benefit for Lumi's own garden.

t.Morrow: The Bleak Tower in Morrow, founded partly by refugees from the ruined gardens, could lose some of its herbalists and Fountainhome magicians to the new gardens. Its own herb output would be reduced if the herbalists returned.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is named as the territory the Fountainhome Spire magicians fled because of Grendel aggression and echoes of madness.
t.Zenith: Zenith could see the Gardens of Pallas rebuilt, with options to give herbs to every herb garden and mana site in the territory. The Fountainhome option would also improve the general standard of life there.

r.Morrow/Ravion: Lutomysla visited Ravion to speak with the Bleak Tower's magicians and botanists. She found that most were unwilling to return to Zenith, though a few might be persuaded by a Synod mandate.
r.Zenith/Iteri: Iteri was the site of the original Gardens of Pallas, now wholly destroyed, and the default location if they are simply rebuilt.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Proceris was proposed as a new home for the gardens, linked to the Golden Cascade's irrigation. There nine mithril monoliths would harness the lingering Druj Night magic to grow realmsroot.

Rings and crowns.d: Urizen, Varushka and the League gained the ability to answer Highborn mandates in their own assemblies, but the League refused all Highborn aid. The Seventh Wave found a Grendel espionage ring in Necropolis that relies on bribed locals. A proposed Highborn mandate would let the army root it out, and similar rings are likely elsewhere on the Bay. Isaac of the Silent Tide destroyed the remaining pillars in Clypion. The Hall of the Newborn Sun gave an original Atun's Ring for the Conclave to endow. Bastion's sacred city still lacks a design, and the League opposes it. The Court ruled the Virtue Fund withdrawals unconstitutional, and stipend motions will follow.

n.Dawn: Pontius Figures of a Dawnish organisation raised the judgement of rewarding seeking Virtue Fund money for Bastion's white granite, which prompted the Court's review. Dawn remains one of five nations Highguard may still aid.
n.Druj: The last major Druj miasma pillars in Zenith were destroyed by Highborn priests, ending the lingering aura they left in the territory.
n.Grendel: Grendel spymasters were found to have built a well-established espionage ring in Necropolis, using merchants and money to buy information from locals. Similar rings are suspected across the Bay of Catazar before the peace treaty ends.
n.Highguard: Highguard extended its peerless kinship across the Empire and uncovered Grendel spies in Necropolis. It may empower the Seventh Wave by mandate, and it was offered a counter-mandate against League involvement in the Bastion project.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the five nations Highguard can still offer its peerless kinship to.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar helped the Marches secure the borders of Bregasland, a territory the Jotun held.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: listed among the nations that have already received Highborn aid.
n.The Brass Coast: The Highborn offered the Freeborn their insight in Kahraman and their strength in retaking Feroz. Madruga is thought likely to host a Grendel espionage ring.
n.The League: The League Assembly refused all Highborn aid and denounced the Bastion project, with a mandate proposed to keep its citizens from helping. Ophelia's mission lets League priests answer Highborn mandates, and Sarvos and possibly Tassato and Spiral may harbour Grendel spies.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Highborn working with Varushka are said to have found their own answer to the question of Thule virtue.
n.Urizen: Urizeni priests can now answer Highborn mandates in their own assembly, and Zenith is free of miasma. The Hall of the Newborn Sun gave an original Atun's Ring in gratitude, and Redoubt likely hosts Grendel spies.
n.Varushka: Highborn unconquered, magisters and wayfarers aided Varushka in seeking out the orcs of its forests and securing its eastern borders. Anastasiya Volkov's mission lets Varushkan priests answer Highborn mandates.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the five nations Highguard can still offer its peerless kinship to.

t.Bastion: The grand project to rebuild Bastion as a beacon of the Way still awaits a chosen design and cannot yet be commissioned. The League Assembly urged its citizens not to aid it.
t.Bay of Catazar: Grendel merchants and navies have visited every Imperial port along the Bay since the treaty, and espionage networks are thought likely throughout its shores.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar accompanied the Marches in securing Bregasland's borders.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn offered their strength to help the Freeborn retake Feroz.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn offered their insight to the Freeborn in Kahraman.
t.Madruga: Grendel navies have been sighted off Madruga, and it is considered almost certain to harbour a Grendel espionage ring.
t.Morrow: The Hall of the Newborn Sun, refugees from Occursion now settled in south-eastern Morrow, offered a gift of thanks for freeing Zenith from miasma. Most of its members chose to stay in Morrow for now.
t.Necropolis: The Seventh Wave, resupplying here, uncovered a long-established Grendel espionage ring that uses bribed locals and merchants. It will be far harder to root out than an ordinary spy network.
t.Redoubt: Grendel navies have visited Redoubt, and an espionage ring there is thought almost certain.
t.Sarvos: Grendel ships have visited Sarvos and spies are likely there. Sarvosan priests led the League's rejection of Highborn aid and its criticism of Bastion.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: there may be Grendel spies in Spiral that Salt Lord Kaliact is unaware of.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato might possibly host Grendel spies, depending on whether the Salt Lords count it as part of the Bay.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Seventh Wave fought in the Barrens' liberation from the Druj, and Highborn are said to be talking with orcs there.
t.Zenith: The last of the Druj miasma faded from Zenith after the remaining pillars were destroyed, completing work begun by the Senate and General Asenath.

r.Necropolis/Longbeach: Mentioned in passing: not named directly, but it lies within Necropolis, where the Grendel espionage ring is spread across the territory.
r.Necropolis/Sanctuary Sand: Mentioned in passing: Sanctuary is named as a place where visiting Grendel sailors could have been reporting to a spymaster.
r.Zenith/Clypion: Isaac of the Silent Tide led priests, exorcists, guardians and cataphracts to Clypion and destroyed the last major Druj miasma pillars there.
r.Zenith/Occursion: Mentioned in passing: the Hall of the Newborn Sun's original temple stood in Occursion before the Druj came.

Ruin.d: The lesser conjunction distorted divination. Cast Off the Chain of Memory, performed at the Imperial regio with iridescent gloaming, swapped a written memory for a strange new one. A musical crescendo would block Swim Leviathan's Depth, Clear Counsel of the Everflowing River and Combing the Beach on the Sunday. On the Saturday of the solstice, the greater conjunction let ritualists who bled and then collapsed gain +1 rank for rituals that call violent entities. It also stirred family conflicts. Three bands of unknown, merciless attackers threatened the Aviary of Ishal, the prime Harp of Astolat and the Pool of Silver Clouds. The Raven Seer, the High Bard and the Dean of the Thorned Rose were each charged with interception through the Sentinel Gate.

n.Dawn: A minor Dawnish house celebrating the Barrens victory was slaughtered or put to flight by the attackers. House Cadence's knights and witches were riding to defend Weaving, and the prime Harp of Astolat lay in the warriors' path.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish house that was attacked had been celebrating the victory in the Barrens.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr vates' visions said their only hope was to send a messenger to Casinea to warn the Dean of the Thorned Rose.
n.Navarr: The vates of the Pool of Silver Clouds foresaw their own murders and the destruction of the Pool. They sent word that the attackers had to be stopped at the Verdant Grove, and the Dean of the Thorned Rose, Bledri Eternal, was charged with protecting them.
n.The League: The third band of attackers emerged in the foothills of central Locul in Temeschwar before heading for Miaren. A League character's marriage ring was also given as an example of a personal omen.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Prognosticator Ingvarn Thunderbrow wondered whether the mysterious attackers might have something to do with the Thule.
n.Wintermark: Attackers butchered the garrison of a Skymark beacon and marched on the Aviary of Ishal, where contact with seers including Maiko Greywolf was lost. The Raven Seer, Odelia Nelda, was made responsible for its defence.

t.Astolat: A band of attackers crossed Astolat in a straight line towards the town of Weaving and the prime Harp of Astolat. The harp's destruction could derange the whole web of harps and disrupt mana production in the territory.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Miaren vates divined that they had to send a messenger to Casinea to tell the Dean of the Thorned Rose of their visions.
t.Kallavesa: Attackers emerged in northern Skymark, wiped out a beacon garrison and headed for Ishal and its Aviary of raven seers.
t.Miaren: The vates and the Pool of Silver Clouds faced destruction, which could only be averted by intercepting the attackers at the Verdant Grove.
t.Temeschwar: The third band of mysterious attackers was reported to have emerged in the foothills of central Locul.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: a Dawnish minor house was celebrating the victory in the Barrens when the attackers struck it.

r.Astolat/Winterbourne: The Sentinel Gate was to open to the Gardens of House Cadence at 18:00 on the Saturday so heroes could protect the prime harp.
r.Kallavesa/Skymark: Attackers came south from northern Skymark after butchering a beacon garrison, and the Sentinel Gate was to open to Maiko's Copse at 17:30 on the Saturday to intercept them.
r.Miaren/Goldglades: The Pool of Silver Clouds and its vates were the target, and the Sentinel Gate was to open to the Verdant Grove in northern Goldglades at 18:30 on the Saturday.
r.Temeschwar/Locul: The third group of blue-sashed attackers emerged in the foothills of central Locul before threatening Miaren.

Sense and sensibility.d: At midnight each night a glowing, idealised miner struck the Ore Hills with a flaming pickaxe and left a rune of Feresh hanging in the sky. The vision faded by the Summer Solstice. Some saw it as a reminder of the 326YE miners' uprising and the push for miners to vote. Mine-captain Jedediah Boon was urged to have the uprising's leaders researched and recognised for virtue. Some Mournwold Orcs feared it meant they were unwelcome, so a delegation including Hap the Soft planned to attend Anvil. A Synod mandate was offered that would encourage young orcs to join itinerant harvest labour across the Marches. A few romantics read the vision as a love story.

n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Synod's view that the Imperial Orcs' understanding of their souls holds for all orcs is cited as the obstacle to the Mournwold Orcs joining the Marches, and northern Marchers are said to know only the Sunstorm sept.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Mournwold Orcs are former Jotun thralls who cannot go back, since their resistance to Eisa Winterborn's raid means many Jotun would treat them as oathbreakers.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the welcome the Navarr gave Great Forest Orcs settling in Hercynia and Miaren is contrasted with the Mournwold Orcs' slow acceptance.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: neighbouring Kahraman is noted as sharing the Mournwold's rich veins of green iron.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: news of the League's treatment of the Apulian Orcs unsettles the Mournwold Orcs, and Tassato's presses print lurid ringblack tales about the golden miner.
n.The Marches: The vision revived divisions over whether miners should vote, the status of the Mournwold Orcs and their religious obstacles. The Marcher assembly was offered a mandate to welcome young orcs as itinerant labourers across the nation.

t.Bregasland: Young Mournwolders, possibly including orcs, planned to seek seasonal farm work here, where restoring the land after the Jotun invasion promises plenty of labour.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the places where Great Forest Orcs were welcomed by the Navarr.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: cited as a neighbour sharing the Mournwold's green iron deposits.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the places where Great Forest Orcs were welcomed by the Navarr.
t.Mitwold: Folk from Mitwold travelled to gawk at the vision, and young Mournwolders planned to seek harvest work on its farms. Orc labourers on the Black Canal linking it to the Mournwold had already begun to accustom locals to working alongside orcs.
t.Mournwold: The nightly vision drew sightseers and complaints about lost sleep. It rekindled bad blood between miners and farmers, and between the territory's human and orc neighbours.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: its printing presses churned out lurid ringblack tales about the golden miner, and it is rumoured among Mournwold orcs to take anyone in.
t.Upwold: Visitors from Upwold came to see the vision, and young Mournwolders planned to travel there as itinerant farm labourers.

r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: The wealthy farmers of Chalkdowns, raided in the 326YE uprising, still resent the Ore Hills' songs mourning the executed ringleaders, and old tensions are growing louder.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: Freemoor's farmers, on the opposite side of the old conflict from the mine owners, find the miner vision reviving grievances from the 326YE uprising.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: The vision erupted nightly from the heart of the Ore Hills, disturbing sleep and livestock. Its miners, including Jedediah Boon of the Boon County Miners, saw it as a possible rallying cry for enfranchisement.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Home to mine owners at the heart of the old enfranchisement struggle, sometimes called the Southmoor Uprising, Southmoor finds those rumblings stirred again by the vision.

Shallows and miseries.d: The Black Thorns, Isaella's Dance, Fire of the South, Burning Falcon, Fist of the Mountains and Drakes reclaimed the Jade Range and Braydon's Jasse. Most Jotun had already withdrawn, but a handpicked garrison of Orchard's Watch veterans died almost to the last orc at Fort Braydon. The fort is technically destroyed, held up only by fading Summer magic, and can be saved at the Summer Solstice. Eisa Winterborn sacked Cevia and destroyed the Sapphire Stair. Yanya Uranduln raided the Mournwold and stole mithril and weirwood. Stephen of Sarcombe broke the Spider's Dream. Geht Aran seized Bourse mithril and white granite. Around a thousand Jotun and no more than two hundred Imperial soldiers died.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are cited as the kind of enemy who might simply have collapsed or flooded the Singing Caves, unlike the Jotun.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are recalled as having tried and failed to destroy the Spider's Dream five years earlier.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the only link is the note that Eisa Winterborn helped bring down the western end of Pakaanan's Pass the year before.
n.Jotun: The Jotun abandoned their conquests in Kahraman, losing perhaps a thousand warriors, mostly in a chosen last stand at Fort Braydon. Their raiding warbands carried off thralls, Bourse materials and weirwood, and remaining bands under Geht Aran, Tora Helmhand, Magnus Ironarm and Jarl Haakon offer battle at the Solstice.
n.Navarr: Isaella's Dance and the Black Thorns fought to reclaim Kahraman, with Isaella's Dance killing ruthlessly using Spring magic and poisons. Both armies were hunted by the heralds of Hayaak, who still managed to bring down some of their warriors.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn armies helped reclaim Kahraman. The Fire of the South fought under a merciless Winter enchantment, and the Burning Falcon fought alongside heralds of Eleonaris and Janon. However, Fort Braydon now teeters on collapse, Bourse caravans were robbed and the Spider's Dream was cut, isolating the nation from the League.
n.The League: League lands suffered heavily. Cevia was sacked, about a hundred and fifty people were taken as thralls, the Sapphire Stair was destroyed and the Red Rock mural defaced. Raiders also attacked Trivento and seized League citizens there.
n.The Marches: The Drakes marched south to aid the Freeborn. Meanwhile Yanya Uranduln's raiders struck the Mournwold, stealing mithril and the weirwood for Lowther's Lift and carrying off a few score Marchers. The traitor Stephen of Sarcombe led the attack on the Spider's Dream.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the general of the Fist of the Mountains credits Urizen with entrusting the army with its magical prowess.
n.Wintermark: The Fist of the Mountains fought for glory rather than slaughter in reclaiming the Jade Range and took part in the storming of Fort Braydon. Wintermarkers recalled the Jarl of Kierheim's words explaining the garrison's death-seeking stand.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: five of the armies came to Kahraman fresh from its liberation, and some Drakes wished they were still there finishing the conquest.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman was entirely liberated and is Imperial again, but Fort Braydon is technically destroyed. Mithril and white granite caravans were robbed, and battles at Fort Braydon and Redgate Pass may decide the fort's survival and the security of its western border.
t.Liathaven: The Jotun invasion came out of Liathaven, and the raiders and retreating armies withdrew back into it. Geht Aran's band passed through Redgate Pass towards the Glade of Dead Night to perform his Twelve Breaths ritual.
t.Madruga: Stephen of Sarcombe's warband crossed Madruga to wreck the Spider's Dream, which now forces armies crossing to or from Tassato or Sarvos to halt. A remaining Jotun force threatens Trajadoz.
