t.Mournwold: Yanya Uranduln's thousand-strong raid hit the Singing Caves, stealing mithril and the weirwood for Lowther's Lift and plundering farms. Miners, yeomanry, garrisons and some Mournwold orcs resisted until the raiders withdrew with a few score thralls.
t.Reinos: The House of Fire and Flame proposes collapsing Red Pinnacle, which stands where Reinos, Liathaven and Kahraman meet, to seal the passes. A looted relic, the Overflowing Platter, has ended up among the Jotun of Beatriz's Field.
t.Sarvos: Raiders crossed the Spider's Dream to attack Trivento, damaging businesses and taking a score or more League citizens as thralls. The ruined bridge now cuts Sarvos off from Madruga for traders and armies.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Eisa Winterborn's successes in Sermersuaq are said to have made her warband mighty.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: Eisa's omen urges her to show the southern Empire what the people of Skallahn can bring, and the Towers of Calx and Coom are noted as aiding the Jotun there.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Eisa Winterborn is noted as one of those who brought down the western end of Pakaanan's Pass last year.
t.Tassato: Eisa Winterborn's raiders sacked Cevia, took about a hundred and fifty thralls, destroyed the Sapphire Stair and defaced the Red Rock. Tassatan fleet owners suffer until the locks are rebuilt, and a splinter band under Magnus Ironarm threatens the Arratan Gamble.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs and the Quiet Step withdrew from Kahraman, heading north toward Upwold.

r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: Imperial armies stormed Fort Braydon and wiped out its Jotun garrison. The fort survives only through fading Summer magic, and casting Hammer of the Brilliant Shore at Destrillo Kahras offers a chance to save it.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: The Burning Falcon, Fist of the Mountains and allied armies reclaimed the Jade Range plains as the Jotun retreated towards the Jasse hills.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: Geht Aran's orcs seized caravans carrying mithril from the Great Mine of Briante, though the mine itself was undamaged.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: Caravans of white granite from the Damatian Cliffs were seized by Geht Aran's raiders. The House of Fire and Flame proposes collapsing Red Pinnacle to seal the passes into Serra Damata.
r.Liathaven/Beacon Point: Collapsing Red Pinnacle at Redgate Pass would block the route into Beacon Point and prevent armies moving between it and Kahraman.
r.Liathaven/Liaven's Glen: Mentioned in passing: the great Jotun armies that swept out of Liaven's Glen retreated back the way they came.
r.Madruga/Torres: Stephen of Sarcombe's warband crossed the Torres plains to reach the Spider's Dream. A Jotun force still roams Torres towards Trajadoz, which the Marracossa Sendito must stop.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: Mentioned in passing: Jarl Haakon is recalled as having led his warband into Alderly forest three times in search of the Feni.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Yanya Uranduln's raiders spilled across the Greensward, raiding farms and villages, while a small group visited the burial mound and apple trees near Overton.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Jotun raiders attacked farms, villages and caravans across Southmoor. Jarl Haakon is now secretly building supply caches there for a future invasion, which the Bailiff of the Downs must stop.
r.Reinos/Bastasor: Jotun at Beatriz's Field hold the Overflowing Platter looted from a slain priest, and the General of the Red Wind Corsairs is charged with recovering it.
r.Sarvos/Bocche: Raiders crossing the Spider's Dream struck at Trivento across the Vassa, seizing caravans and League thralls before the bridge's middle-west span fell.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: Mentioned in passing: Eisa Winterborn is noted as having helped bring down the western end of the pass last year.
r.Tassato/Cascatas: Eisa Winterborn's raiders overwhelmed Cevia, took around a hundred and fifty thralls, destroyed the centuries-old Sapphire Stair locks and defaced the Red Rock with a walrus and the Rune of Victory.
r.Tassato/Enterio: The Sentinel Gate opens to Duarte's Repose so the Custodian of the Arratan Gamble can stop Magnus Ironarm's band before it raids the Gamble for white granite and thralls.

Taken at the flood.d: Six armies (the Golden Sun, Golden Axe, Citadel Guard, Valiant Pegasus, Winter Sun and Iron Helms) advanced from the Towers of Dusk. The Druj armies had fled to the Mallum, leaving only warbands and holdouts. Their parting curses brought a devastating deluge, Spring-bound killer trees and malign Winter spirits. A Dawnish enchantment spread black roses, and a desiccating wind withered the Bleaks and Farweald. Druj resistance remains only in Murderdale and the Heart of Peytaht. The Karass refuse to co-operate, the Vendarri seek control of the Saltmarsh, and the Rahvin hold the Fangs. Three conjunctions offer chances to rescue Montanians, stop Varag Soulflayer and protect the Great Forest elders.

n.Dawn: With the Barrens newly allocated to Dawn, the Golden Sun ground forward alongside the Knights of Glory and the servants of the Bound King, whose clashes forced the Dawnish to keep them apart, while three Dawnish covens spread black roses in the armies' wake.
n.Druj: The Druj armies fled to the Mallum and left only holdouts in Murderdale and the Heart of Peytaht, but their ghulai unleashed a final barrage of curses and their warbands still threaten Montanian captives and the Great Forest elders.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Winter Sun led the effort to free the Druj slaves and met a mixed reception, and the Menrothat reminded the Varushkans of the offer they had made the Imperial Orcs regarding Farweald.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Thunderous Tread of the Trees raging across Jotun-held Liathaven is compared with the Druj tree-spirits.
n.Navarr: The Senator for Therunin, Travid Longest Path, is charged with stopping a Druj force in the Heart of Peytaht, and success would see the Great Forest elders teach Navarr armies how to cross the Great Forest.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Druj binding of Spring spirits into trees is described as the first since Holberg.
n.Urizen: The Citadel Guard advanced steadily through the Bleaks and Farweald, ignored the Synod's call to act as liberators, and its scholars noted a surge of new Winter regio across the Barrens.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe and the Iron Helms fought at the forefront of the advance but disregarded the Synod, and the Menrothat of Ossium sent emissaries to remind their Varushkan neighbours of the offer regarding Farweald.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is cited as the last time the Druj bound killer spirits into trees.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Thunderous Tread of the Trees is noted as currently raging across Liathaven.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Menrothat of Ossium sent emissaries to the Varushkans about their offer concerning Farweald.
t.The Barrens: All of the Barrens except Murderdale and the Heart of Peytaht came under Imperial control, but the territory was ravaged by floods, killer trees, Winter spirits and spreading Winter regio, with heavy losses among both Dawnish and orc civilians.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Senator for Therunin is made responsible for stopping the Druj in the Heart of Peytaht.

r.The Barrens/Farweald: Farweald was conquered but scarred by a desiccating wind, and the Menrothat are pressing their earlier offer concerning the region.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: Druj holdouts, reinforced by orcs fleeing Dawnguard, remain here, and a Druj band with heralds of Surut is moving to slaughter the elders of the Great Forest Orcs.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: A Druj force has captured Montanians, including Circe the Strider, to turn them into tortured souls, and the General of the Valiant Pegasus is asked to rout them.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Murderdale remains outside Imperial control, held by Druj holdouts reinforced by orcs fleeing Dawnguard, though they could do little to delay a renewed advance.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: A further magical tempest worsened the drowned marshes and caused deaths at the Fangs, still held by the Rahvin, while the Vendarri seek concessions ceding the Saltmarsh largely to their control.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: The Groves were conquered after Druj Spring wards claimed Imperial lives, but Varag Soulflayer is moving to a Winter regio there to release a Dream of Famine.

The current when it serves.d: More than fifteen thousand Imperial soldiers gathered at the Fortress of Kalant. They then followed Emperor Guntherm's old route into Skallahn. Jotun beacons gave early warning, but the defenders were overwhelmed. The Winterfolk fought honourably and quarter was given on both sides, while terrified thralls mostly fled west. Greenwall fell within a month and Jarl Asbjørn Dalgaard retreated to Bjarkey. Iron Stand was half taken by the Solstice, and aid was rumoured from Tromsa and Hordalant. Blade Quencher's Hall began growing and attacking Imperial troops. A battle was offered to sever or destroy its regio and kill Blade Quencher. Conjunctions offered the chance to recover Blerung's shield and to stop Greenwall's fyrd forming.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Summer Storm advanced steadily into Skallahn to free thralls, guided by the voice of Sjöfn of the Bittenblade. Its General was charged with stopping Jarl Asbjørn Dalgaard from raising Greenwall's fyrd at Paegga's Rest.
n.Jotun: The Jotun were caught outmatched on their home ground, losing Greenwall and half of Iron Stand. However, reinforcements were reportedly coming from Tromsa and Hordalant, and Blade Quencher's Autumn warriors rallied routed warbands at his Hall.
n.Wintermark: The Bloodcloaks and Green Shield led the offensive and fought as heroes, offering quarter and insisting that their allies fight honourably. Blerunning Hall asked the Watcher of Britta's Pool to recover Blerung the Bright Lantern's lost shield.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: General Styx recalled the Summer Storm's earlier fighting in Bregasland to push back the Jotun.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: scouts reported orc forces crossing from Hordalant, probably to defend Skallahn.
t.Kallavesa: Blerung the Bright Lantern's effects rest in Kallavesa's marshes. If her lost shield is recovered and given to a host of Sulkavaris, it can be laid there beside her.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: the Sea of Snow is not named on the page, which concerns the land campaign in neighbouring Skallahn.
t.Sermersuaq: The invasion was launched from Sermersuaq, and the armies in Iron Stand rely on its border for reinforcement and retreat. Blade Quencher's Hall threatens the supply routes back into the territory.
t.Skallahn: Skallahn was invaded by the Empire for the first time in a generation; Greenwall was claimed as a beachhead and Iron Stand was half conquered. Blade Quencher's expanding Hall threatened to undo these gains and strengthen the Jotun.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: scouts reported scattered aid being sent south by the Jarls of Tromsa to Skallahn.

r.Sermersuaq/Stark: The three armies gathered and planned the offensive at the Fortress of Kalant in Stark. Blade Quencher's fane stands right on Stark's border.
r.Skallahn/Bjarkey: Jarl Asbjørn Dalgaard retreated to Bjarkey after losing Greenwall. He was awaiting the Greenwall fyrd at Paegga's Rest, where the Summer Storm's General could intercept him.
r.Skallahn/Greenwall: Greenwall fell to the Empire within a month and most of its thralls fled. Blade Quencher's Hall threatens the Imperial beachhead there unless it is severed from Autumn or its regio destroyed.
r.Skallahn/Iron Stand: The armies pushed into Jarl Ebbe of Overgaard's lands around the ruined Iron Banner and held half the region by the Solstice. Blerung's lost shield is held by a ghodi at Kevan's Holt there.

The deepest cut.d: Although Sulemaine was never recognised by the Synod, her uniquely Urizen status means only the Urizen Assembly can mandate her tomb. A consecration to Wisdom, Ambition, Courage, Pride or Vigilance would permanently free Urizen from General, Nine and virtue assembly statements and mandates. A Wisdom aura would also bring a flowering of philosophy and let the Arbiter of the Four Winds oppose one Synod mandate each season. Clytemnestra's alternative Wisdom mandate would instead end the rift with the Synod. Severus of the Blinding Sun offered a consecration to Hate, allowing a second Urizen army but cutting Doyen of the Spires ranks. The Synod's only counters were declaring her a false paragon or removing the aura.

n.Highguard: Sulemaine hunted and executed Highborn missionaries and is widely seen as a murderous villain there. Hazelelponi offered a Highguard Assembly mandate to lead pilgrims to the tomb, which would likely turn Highborn opinion strongly against Urizen.
n.Urizen: The Urizen Assembly alone decides the tomb's fate. Most consecrations would permanently put the nation beyond the reach of most Synod assemblies, Clytemnestra's mandate would reconcile it with the Synod, and a Hate aura would raise a sword-scholar army at the cost of the Doyen of the Spires.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: cited as a nation where Sulemaine is not well known.

t.Morrow: Sulemaine's burial site lies in Morrow, where the tomb would be consecrated. Any Synod attempt to strip its aura would face sword scholars there and need an Imperial army escort.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Urizen statements also urged the faithful to go on to Zenith to witness the Crucible of Fate being consecrated to Prosperity.

r.Morrow/Peregro: The caverns Herminius excavated in Peregro are confirmed as Sulemaine's resting place and haunted by at least two ghosts of her followers. Severus of the Blinding Sun wanders the region.
r.Zenith/Iteri: Mentioned in passing: the newly built Crucible of Fate in Iteri was named as the site for a separate consecration to Prosperity by Bartimaeus of Zenith Ascendant.

The fate of the many.d: Unless the Assembly intervened, most Urizeni would leave Spiral for Zenith, Morrow and Redoubt, abandoning its spires. The Assembly could back one of several competing mandates. Caela of the Tower of the Silver Flame urged people to stay until the League lost Spiral to the Grendel, which would weaken the Citadel Guard there. Agathea urged magicians to join the League and shape Apulian. Hector of Tropaion's alternative proposed staying apart in enclaves. Separate mandates would either share the secret of the Block with the League or withhold all aid; if neither passed, new commissions there would cost 25% more in labour. Sadogua offered to move one thing out of Spiral. Sung offered to create an Oblivion Sentinel title and mithril sculptures.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: bitter Urizeni compared the loss of Spiral to the "theft" of Holberg from Dawn.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua is noted for past boons helping Urizen against the Druj.
n.Grendel: With the peace treaty about to end, Caela predicted a Grendel invasion of Spiral to punish Kaliact's followers. The Urizen had never shared the secret of the Block with them, though sharing it with the League would likely spread it to the Grendel too.
n.The League: The League was taking on a territory its Urizeni residents largely resented. Its fate there could turn on whether Urizen magicians joined it in Apulian, shared the secret of the Block, or withheld aid, raising building costs and cutting taxation.
n.Urizen: Urizen faced losing a land it had claimed since before the Empire. Its Assembly had to choose between mandates to stay, join the League, or secede in enclaves, while Sung offered a new national title of Oblivion Sentinel to keep watch over the Black Plateau.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: its transfer from Dawn to the League was invoked in bitter comparisons with the loss of Spiral.
t.Morrow: Morrow was one of the destinations for Urizeni leaving Spiral, and its legacy would be bolstered by the newcomers' ideas.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt would receive many Urizeni emigrants from Spiral. If the Senate created Sung's title, a mithril sculpture would be placed in its peaks above the Brilliant Star, and Caela predicted that a Grendel-held Spiral would threaten it.
t.Spiral: Spiral's Urizeni faced mass emigration that would leave its spires silent unless the Assembly gave them a plan. Its future also hung on competing mandates over staying, joining the League, secession and the secret of the Block.
t.Zenith: Zenith, now the Crucible of Fate, was expected to gain brilliant minds from Spiral. It could host one of Sung's mithril sculptures and perhaps the remains of Damakhan's Forge if Sadogua moved them.

r.Redoubt/Optarion: A mithril sculpture would stand in the peaks of Optarion above the Brilliant Star if the Senate created the Oblivion Sentinel title.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Attention was shifting to the burgeoning City of Apulian. Agathea, an architect still dwelling in Apulus, urged Urizen magicians to join the League and shape the city with philosophy and learning.
r.Spiral/Screed: The baleful influence of the Black Plateau in Screed drove much of the exodus. Sung offered to make the hidden spire of Oblivion's Edge the base of a new Oblivion Sentinel watching over it.
r.Zenith/Proceris: A mithril sculpture would be placed at the northern end of the Twilight Gate in southern Proceris, aligned with Oblivion's Edge, if the Senate created the Oblivion Sentinel title.

The horror and the wild.d: Tales spread of miraculous recoveries and sudden riches, but also of a vanished vale and a Navarr wayhouse swallowed by the Semmerlak. Dho'uala's drowned emissaries demanded that criminals be cast into the lake and that theft from its depths cease. The Senate could pass laws on either point, and Dawnish, Varushkan and Holberg fleets remained penalised. Three opportunities arose: Irina's Grove in Skoremujac, where trapped mora trade herbs; a slaughterhouse at Tolvoli to feed blood-hungry dubik in exchange for potions; and the Deep Place at Void, where cabalists offer tempest jade. In northern Weirwater, the village of Surlac had been abandoned, and the Schlacta of Rot demanded both a Dawnish and a Varushkan champion.

n.Dawn: Dawnish fleets on the Semmerlak still suffered from Dho'uala's disruption, and Varushkan merchants taught a sceptical Dawn how to deal with the sovereign. Dawnish heroes were also needed at Surlac and to supply a champion against the Deadwood Knight.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: two members of the doomed wagon-raider band were said to have died in Ossium fighting the Druj.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: a lakeside Navarr wayhouse in Karov was swallowed by the Semmerlak overnight, leaving forty people unaccounted for.
n.The League: Holberg fleets continued to suffer a production penalty from Dho'uala's disruption of the Semmerlak. Holberg was also among the territories where a proposed law would have criminals drowned in the lake.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: a fabled tunnel was said to run beneath the mountains of Brez into Thule-held Otkodov.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: one of the wagon raiders was said to have died in Urizen-held Zenith fighting the Wolves of War.
n.Varushka: The Assembly's call to bargain with dark powers brought Varushkans both windfalls and disasters. It also opened opportunities at Irina's Grove, Tolvoli and Void, and left Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti responsible for meeting the Schlacta of Rot's challenge.

t.Holberg: Holberg's Semmerlak fleets remained penalised, and the Senate could direct magistrates there to execute criminals by drowning in the lake.
t.Karov: A Navarr wayhouse on Karov's shore vanished beneath the Semmerlak, and Irina's Grove offered a commission opportunity. The Deadwood Knight stirred in the southern woods, and a law against taking from the lake would hit Karov's fishing.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Karsk was listed among the Semmerlak territories where a proposed law would have criminals drowned in the lake.
t.Miekarova: Dubik nesting among the ruins of the Heart of the Tempest had begun trading potions for animal blood. Wagon raiders proposed a slaughterhouse at Tolvoli to keep the dubik supplied.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium was named as a battleground where two raiders died against the Druj, and was listed for the proposed drowning law.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov was the rumoured end of a mythical tunnel beneath the mountains of Brez.
t.Semmerholm: Varushkan merchants explained Dho'uala to the people of Semmerholm. The territory was named in the proposed drowning law and would lose fishing revenue if taking from the lake were outlawed.
t.The Semmerlak: Dho'uala's drowned emissaries appeared on ships' decks demanding that the condemned be drowned and theft from the depths stop. Port expansion around the lake was impossible while the disruption lasted.
t.Volodmartz: The cabalists of Void in Volodmartz sought help to build the Deep Place in exchange for tempest jade. Separately, a wagon raider was said to have died in a wayhouse brawl in Volodmartz.
t.Weirwater: Varushkan advice on Dho'uala found a receptive audience in Weirwater. Two conjunctions threatened its north: the abandoned village of Surlac and the Deadwood Knight's challenge.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: a wagon raider named Olag Gannovic was said to have died in Zenith fighting the Wolves of War.

r.Karov/Skoremujac: Hunters found mora trapped in a delusion of village life at Irina's Grove, trading herbs for trinkets. Restoring the grove's paths would create a Tender of Irina's Grove, an opportunity open until the end of the Summer Solstice.
r.Miekarova/Mieriada: Wagon raiders from Tolvoli proposed a slaughterhouse to feed the nearby dubik in exchange for Bloodwine Liquor, Blackblood Thorns and Darkwine. Unless it was completed by the Winter Solstice, the dubik might turn to human blood.
r.Miekarova/Perumaki: Mentioned in passing: the former guardians of Irina's Grove died fighting a plaguewulf in Perumaki.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: The cabalists of Void apparently struck a bargain with something malignant beneath the peaks of Brez. They offered tempest jade to a Bredavoi Emissary if the Deep Place was commissioned by the end of the Autumn Equinox.
r.Weirwater/Sandling: The people of Surlac fled to the hills after something began picking them off. A Sentinel Gate conjunction let five people investigate under Areloe Larmallevés.
r.Weirwater/Wickmoor: The Schlacta of Rot emerged in the woods on the Karov border, demanding a Dawnish and a Varushkan champion. Twenty heroes could reach it through a conjunction, and if the challenge went unmet it would begin a murderous rampage.

Three and three.d: Estavus declined to parley and instead sent servants to help rebuild Zenith and Urizen. She also said the Empire should make the offer if it wants her to staff a fane. Azoth agreed to a parley about the Last Singing Stone, the Tower of Light and Shadow and Skywise Gralka's ideas, and asked the Conclave to interdict Mark the Flesh Incorruptible. Eleonaris replied for Hayaak, who refuses all parley until Edric deGauvin is executed, and offered Blaze Dunning a trial of service. Wise Rangara agreed to parley but would not discuss herb lore. Siakha refused a formal parley but will meet the Spring Archmage at Azcara's Field. An unknown eternal agreed to parley with the Archmage of Day.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Wise Rangara mocked the Empire's belief that the Druj know more herb lore than it does, suggesting it simply keep fighting them and take that lore.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Siakha's chosen meeting place, Azcara's Field near the ruins of Shantarim, lies in Grendel-held Feroz.
n.Jotun: Hayaak, the Knight of Hawks, has sworn to support the Jotun on every battlefield where they fight the Empire until Edric deGauvin is executed. Blaze Dunning could only be his champion by renouncing the Empire and fighting alongside the Jotun.
n.Navarr: Azoth wants to discuss the Last Singing Stone with the Advisor on the Vallorn, suggesting its power might be unlocked for the Navarr nation's use and testing how adaptable the Navarr truly are.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: there were unreliable reports of Siakha's representatives observing League-held Sarvos.
n.Urizen: Estavus sent dozens of Autumn heralds across Urizen, and especially to Zenith and the Crucible of Fate, to aid the nation's rebuilding. Urizeni archmages Elyssiathain and Ematius secured parleys with Azoth and Wise Rangara.
n.Wintermark: Eleonaris offered the Winter-mark hero Blaze Dunning a chance to enter the Lion of Summer's service. She is to face three tests in the Hall of Worlds and must first find a way to get there.

t.Feroz: Siakha's emissaries will meet the Archmage of Spring and her party at Azcara's Field, near the ruins of the corsair town of Shantarim, reached through a Sentinel Gate conjunction. Those staying inside the circle of safety will be unharmed.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: there were unreliable reports that heralds of Siakha had been seen in Sarvos, apparently observing the Empire.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: there were unreliable reports that representatives of Siakha had been seen in Sermersuaq, though their purpose was unclear.
t.Zenith: Dozens of Estavus's heralds descended on Zenith to suggest improvements and help rebuild it and the Crucible of Fate. Heralds of Siakha were also reportedly seen there.

Two minutes.d: Celestial Arch emissaries spent three months with the Tchemetzi family in Pelabuhan. The family offered two vital honey a season for the ritual text of Regrow the Land's Heart, and said they would endorse the Conclave to Ossegrahn if it were given. The Arshlan family provided nine wains of mithril for endowment. The Quiet Hall in Oakways became a hospital for magical ailments, and could be expanded by commission. The Shuttered Lantern destroyed the vis-bleeding rock of ice in Tanikipari, rejecting Blood-on-the-Snow's boons. Sadogua thanked the Conclave. With Navarr guides and the Loyalty Assembly, the Suranni wizards began to find homes across most of the Empire.

n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly sent Exarch Luke to urge wayfarers and magisters to welcome the Suranni. Most refugees rejected these overtures, but Highborn patience has begun to ease their fear, though none will settle in Highguard.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs are listed among the three nations where the Suranni wizards will not settle.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Tchemetzi see Regrow the Land's Heart as useful for Faraden lands ravaged by war with the Jotun.
n.Navarr: Navarr guides sent under Teleri Thornweaver's mandate took in most of the Suranni wizards and found them homes. The Assembly's statement urging conversion to the Way led some stridings and steadings to turn families away until the Loyalty Assembly's backing won them round.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Grandmaster of the Golden Pyramid set the order to support the Crucible of Fate in Zenith.
n.Wintermark: Shuttered Lantern magicians, miners and runesmiths broke apart and boiled away the vis-bleeding rock of ice in Tanikipari. The Celestial Arch's gifts to the Tchemetzi included a wand inscribed by the runesmiths of Kalpaheim.

t.Miaren: The former wayhouse of Harad of the High Path in Miaren became the Quiet Hall, a hospital for those harmed by magic, under the Custodian of the Lost.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: the Celestial Arch delegation endured a freezing, storm-beset crossing of the Sea of Snow to reach Pelabuhan.
t.Sermersuaq: The rock of bleeding ice in Sermersuaq was destroyed, ending a source of Heart's Blood tied to Blood-on-the-Snow.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Shuttered Lantern's recent investigations in Skarsind are what led them to the bleeding ice rock.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Pyramid has been set to support the Crucible of Fate in Zenith.

r.Miaren/Oakways: The Quiet Hall in Oakways now serves as a hospital for magical maladies. It could be expanded with apothecary gardens for 10 weirwood, 20 crowns and three months' work, yielding Magpie and Ravenwing Infusions each season.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: In a secluded Tanikipari valley, miners hired by the Shuttered Lantern broke the bleeding ice boulder into rubble and boiled it to steam, with no sign of any trap or wrath from Agramant.
r.Zenith/Lustri: Mentioned in passing: the page notes Golden Pyramid support for the Crucible of Fate in Zenith but does not name Lustri directly.

Welly boots.d: The Jotun retreated in good order into Hordalant, without their usual promise to return. Mathilda Fisher fled west with a handful of loyal followers when the Empire turned south towards Kahraman, but Bushel Sykes stayed behind. Neighbours who sided with the invaders now face long Bregas grudges. The Marcher National Assembly could pass a mandate witnessing General Amberlain's oath that the Strong Reeds will never abandon Bregasland. The oath brings yeofolk support but carries harsh penalties if broken. The looted Breadbasket could be restocked for 15 thrones or handed to House Greywater. It could also be extended to Mournwold. Sykes has openly appeared at Ottery, creating a probable trap for General Asenath.

n.Jotun: The Jotun abandoned Bregasland in an orderly retreat into Hordalant and took Mathilda Fisher's cause with them, notably without any boast that they would return.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Empire turned its attention south towards Kahraman, which let Mathilda Fisher escape.
n.The Marches: The Marches regain Bregasland but face bitter local grudges and a looted Breadbasket. The National Assembly has the chance to bind the Strong Reeds to Bregasland by oath, to reward House Greywater, or to extend the Breadbasket to Mournwold.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar left Urizen with its work done, and General Asenath credited Urizen and Warcaster Aulus with the speed of her march to the Marches.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland was retaken without a fight as the Jotun and the Fishers fled. Its Breadbasket was left looted, and neighbours who backed opposite sides now nurse grudges. Bushel Sykes remains at large.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun pulled back from Bregasland into Hordalant.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's attention turned south towards Kahraman, giving Mathilda Fisher the chance to flee.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: food to restock the Bregasland Breadbasket would be bought in Upwold and Mitwold.
t.Mournwold: Marchers proposed extending the Breadbasket to Mournwold as a great work costing 35 weirwood, 15 white granite and 100 crowns. It would share 1080 rings among the territory's farms, but would do nothing for its miners.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: in the story, Mathilda's fur cloak was a gift from the Jarl of Tromsa, and Anagar had urged her to stay in Tromsa.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: food to restock the Bregasland Breadbasket would be bought in Upwold and Mitwold.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Mathilda Fisher was cornered at Graven Rock, beaten and ripe for capture, before the Empire's shift south let her slip away.
r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: Mentioned in passing: in the story, Bushel Sykes rows Mathilda through the mists out of the Grey Fens as she escapes.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: Mentioned in passing: Larkin Pewter, a Landskeeper from the North Fens, offered an Autumn charm so the Strong Reeds' oath could be sworn by the Lictors.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: The Granite Pillar force-marched to Ottermire, and Bushel Sykes openly appeared at the Ottery fishing docks. A small Sentinel Gate conjunction there on the Saturday of the summit, assigned to General Asenath, has all the hallmarks of a trap.

Wild blue yonder.d: After a three-day diplomatic silence, the Salt Lords resumed contact without an official response to Spiral becoming a League territory, though merchants hinted at fury and demanded Retribution. The Broken Shore Market and Spiral Envoy positions lapsed. Paymaster Muireall's enclave in southern Apstrus refused Imperial law and taxes, and might open a mountain route from Mareave. Her envoy was due at Anvil. Asavean warships destroyed the Sanctuary of the Justicars and Shantarim, saboteurs burned Sarvos's Cavabianca Docks, and privateers preyed on Liberty Pact shipping in the Bay of Catazar. Faraden ties improved, but a coming Faraden–Jotun meeting threatened overland trade through the Lasambrian Hills. A Freeborn family was rescued from Feroz.

n.Grendel: The Salt Lords were blindsided by Salt Lord Kaliact's defection and are said to want Retribution, while Paymaster Muireall's enclave rejected Imperial rule in Spiral and the Broken Shore Market stood empty. Speaker Morna denied that any Grendel ships were involved in the Asavean attacks.
n.Highguard: Grendel traders and sailors were welcomed in Necropolis under Brother Wildfyre's mandate, despite the Seventh Wave's warnings, and Highborn captains were encouraged to tell of clashes with Asavean pirates. Accalon of Felix's Watch was asked to host the Liberty Pact meetings.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Pakt of the Imperial Orcs was listed as Ambassador to Asavea.
n.Jotun: The Jotun were due to meet the Faraden at the Spring Equinox to renegotiate travel through the Lasambrian Hills. The Lasambrian Jotun reportedly wanted the Faraden to trade only with them, which could end overland Faraden–Imperial trade.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Cedric Gallows and Fintan Nighthaven of Navarr were named as ambassadors to the Iron Confederacy and Axos.
n.The Brass Coast: Suranni lawkeepers continued crossing into Segura after Hand of Dumon cultists, while Faraden trade into the Brass Coast stayed robust. The rescued Kanza family settled in Madruga, and Freeborn corsairs helped contain the Asavean privateers.
n.The League: Spiral was now a League territory, and Apulian traders courted their new fellow citizens. Asavean saboteurs burned the Cavabianca Docks in Sarvos, and Sarvosan captains fought the privateers in the Bay.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Thule appeared only in further reading on trade with Varushka and the Northern trade network.
n.Urizen: Abel of Urizen served as Ambassador to the Grendel and Ariadne as Ambassador to Jarm, while captains sailing from Redoubt helped hold back the Asavean privateers.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka appeared only in a further-reading link about trade opportunities with the Thule.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Eska Crowspeaker of Wintermark was listed as Voice of Liberty.

t.Bay of Catazar: Asavean privateers preyed on Liberty Pact vessels in the Bay, enslaving crews and drowning officers, while Imperial captains largely contained them. Broken Shore merchants kept trading in Imperial ports around it.
t.Feroz: Governor Rahab continued his work in Feroz and reportedly prompted the Asavean raids. The temple delegate Marsail Cailc vanished, and the Kanza family were spirited out of the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull.
t.Madruga: Grendel navies remained moored off the coast, and the rescued Kanza family settled there with mixed feelings about the war with Asavea.
t.Mareave: Muireall's enclave on the Mareave border could open a mountain route from Mareave into Apstrus, letting Grendel forces bypass the Apulian Way. Her envoy came from the North Mareave Trading Consortium.
t.Necropolis: Broken Shore traders and Golden Winds sailors were welcomed in its hostels and inns under Brother Wildfyre's mandate, though the Seventh Wave confirmed that more than traders may be getting in. Captains based there helped contain the privateers.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov was named among the smaller neighbouring nations with outsized influence on the Empire.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: captains operating from Redoubt were among those containing the Asavean privateers.
t.Sarvos: Asavean 'merchant' ships set fire to the Cavabianca Docks, which were destroyed beyond repurposing, though the Sweetwater Springs helped stop the blaze reaching the city. Sarvosan captains also fought the privateers.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: priests of the Pride assembly crossed the Sea of Snow to study the Faraden faith.
t.Segura: Some Suranni merchants still traded overland into Segura, but most border crossers were lawkeepers hunting Hand of Dumon cultists.
t.Spiral: Spiral's new status as a League territory went officially unanswered by the Salt Lords, who are privately enraged. The Spiral Envoy title and the Broken Shore Market lapsed, and Muireall's enclave refused Imperial rule.

r.Spiral/Apstrus: Paymaster Muireall's Grendel enclave in southern Apstrus refused Imperial law and taxes but avoided violence. With her mountaineering gear and experts, she might forge a route through the Apstrus mountains from Mareave.

Windfall.d: The egregores found the Apulians ambitious, competitive and fond of intrigue, and lightly attached to their Grendel faith, but questioned their loyalty after Kaliact betrayed her fellow Salt Lords. With no eligible League business owners in Spiral, the Constitutional Court ruled the Senator for Spiral title did not yet exist, and the election was scheduled for the Autumn Equinox. Imperial law barred recent voters elsewhere from voting there for up to twelve months. Kaliact wanted the territory renamed Apulian, which needs a Senate motion. The Legacy, producing 22 wains of mithril, awaits Senate allocation as an Imperial or League seat. The fortifications Ballaghadruh and the Apulian Palace, garrisoned mostly by Apulian Orcs, passed to the Senate's upkeep.

n.Grendel: Kaliact's followers, who have renounced the Salt Lords of Dubhtraig, were being judged as possible League citizens. They have stopped calling themselves Grendel and now use the name Apulians, and their Grendel faith was raised as a possible obstacle.
n.The League: The League's egregores were to decide at the summit whether to admit the Apulian Orcs. Meanwhile the four existing League senators could make the decisions that need the unanimous agreement of League senators, and League citizens could now move businesses into Spiral.
n.Urizen: Renaming Spiral to Apulian would tell the Urizen living there that any hope of the territory returning to their nation was over. The Apulians suggested working with the Urizen on a joint bid for the Legacy's mithril.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar is not referred to directly in the text.
t.Holberg: The Senator for Holberg was one of the four League senators able to make the decisions that need all League senators to agree. Holberg business owners who move to Spiral cannot vote there until Spring 386YE.
t.Sarvos: It was unclear whether the people of Sarvos would welcome the orcs who had occupied their city. Sarvos business owners who move to Spiral cannot vote there until Summer 386YE, although congregation leaders could buy a business in Spiral and vote normally.
t.Spiral: Spiral became part of the League, but its Senator title was ruled not yet to exist, with an election set for the Autumn Equinox. Kaliact pressed to rename it Apulian, and the Senate took on upkeep of Ballaghadruh and the Apulian Palace.
t.Tassato: The Senator for Tassato could share in the decisions that need all League senators to agree, such as appointing the Steward of the Tassato Mana Exchange. Tassatan business owners who move to Spiral now could vote in its Autumn Equinox election.
t.Temeschwar: The egregores judged the Apulians every bit as ruthless as the Temeschwari. Temeschwar business owners who move to Spiral cannot vote there until Winter 385YE.

r.Spiral/Ossuary: Ossuary holds the Legacy, a great mithril mine producing 22 wains each season. It was technically under Kaliact's control and awaited allocation by the Senate, and any mithril not allocated would be kept for the first person appointed to the seat.
